## 2026-08-30 -- existing streams gained real readiness selection

### Work summary

Moved `stream_select()` into the harvested stream library. The 549-function
ledger is now **232 native, 163 userland and 154 pending**.

Added one `PHP2Go\\Internal\\stream_select()` leaf. It maps php2go's existing
file and standard-stream descriptors through `select(2)` and treats RFC2397
memory handles as immediately readable/writable. The public PHP body owns all
array validation and rebuilding, nullable timeout policy, diagnostics and
by-reference write-back; the leaf creates no socket, wrapper, filter or
transport resource.

The differential also exposed a shared alias boundary: harvested builtin
validation skipped every by-reference parameter type. A wrong value therefore
entered the cloned PHP body and produced user-function wording with a caller
location. By-reference signature checks now run before harvested replacements,
preserving the reference slot. Native implementations still parse their own
by-reference arguments because some deliberately narrow the harvested manifest
shape, as `array_walk()` does.

### Findings

The linked signature has four required and five total parameters: nullable
read, write and exception arrays by reference, nullable seconds, and optional
nullable microseconds. Array contents are examined before timeout values. When
no valid stream exists, even an array made entirely of invalid values produces
`ValueError: No stream arrays were passed`. Once any valid stream exists, a
non-resource produces the `supplied argument` TypeError while a context or
closed handle produces `supplied resource`.

Seconds may be null for an indefinite wait. In that form microseconds must be
null or zero; any nonzero value, including a negative one, earns the
null-with-null-seconds ValueError. With non-null seconds both time components
must be nonnegative, and microseconds above one million are normalized rather
than rejected.

Ready arrays retain their original integer and string keys. Duplicate copies of
one handle remain in the output but count once within a readiness set; the same
handle ready for both read and write counts twice. Rebuilt elements lose input
reference boxes. When the same array variable is supplied to multiple
parameters, read, then write, then exception write-back determines its final
value.

Regular files and RFC2397 handles are readable and writable and are not
exception-ready in the probed cases. An RFC2397 handle remains read-ready at its
end and after EOF has been observed. A ready memory handle makes selection
immediate; an exception-only descriptor waits for the requested timeout and is
then filtered out.

## 2026-08-30 -- assertion options became behavior, not a state facade

### Work summary

Moved `assert_options()` into the harvested standard library. The 549-function
ledger is now **232 native, 162 userland and 155 pending**.

Added one request-local option record behind
`PHP2Go\\Internal\\assert_options()`, and made the existing native `assert()`
path consume it. PHP owns option-number validation and legacy INI-boolean
conversion; the runtime applies active, callback, bail, warning and exception
policy.

This supersedes the earlier rejection of a userland-only `assert_options()`
facade. That rejection remains correct: merely storing values would be false
coverage. The function moved only after its state was wired through every
observable assertion outcome.

### Findings

The linked defaults are active 1, callback null, bail 0, warning 1 and exception
1. Boolean options stringify their input and recognize only `1`, `on`, `yes`
and `true` case-insensitively as true. Arrays raise the ordinary conversion
warning and become false; non-stringable objects raise their conversion Error.
Callback state accepts arbitrary values and is validated only when an assertion
actually fails.

`ASSERT_ACTIVE=0` does not skip evaluation of the assertion expression. The
compiler's `ZEND_ASSERT_CHECK` still admits the expression because
`zend.assertions=1`; the eventual `assert()` call returns true after the
expression has run. This settled the boundary at the native call rather than in
opcode control flow.

A callback receives the public filename, line, null legacy-code slot and the
actual description value. It runs before the warning or exception and can throw.
A missing callback raises `Error: Invalid callback ...`; with no user error
handler and warning mode enabled, the linked engine first prints the assertion
warning, while an installed handler suppresses that warning branch. Both paths
are modeled.

Exception mode throws a supplied Throwable unchanged or creates
`AssertionError` from the description. Without exception mode, warning mode
raises the exact `assert(): ... failed` warning and the call returns false;
warning-off is silent. Bail mode terminates the request after callback/warning
processing. Active-off returns true.

The function deprecation is ordered before parameter parsing. Even missing,
excess and invalid-option calls first emit `Function assert_options() is
deprecated since 8.3`; a narrow pre-validation interpreter hook preserves that
ordering without duplicating the diagnostic in PHP.

## 2026-08-30 -- locality stayed PHP; TTY needed one ioctl bit

### Work summary

Moved `stream_is_local()` and `stream_isatty()` into the harvested streams
library. The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 160 userland and 157
pending**.

`stream_is_local()` required no runtime primitive: PHP parses wrapper schemes
against the already-probed six-wrapper startup registry and reads existing
stream metadata. `stream_isatty()` adds one `TCGETS` boolean operation to the
existing `PHP2Go\\Internal\\stream_operation()` leaf; validation and public
return behavior remain PHP.

### Findings

The locality parameter is intentionally untyped. Non-resources are cast to a
path, including the exact array-to-string warning; objects without
`__toString()` raise their ordinary conversion `Error`. Live non-stream and
closed resources instead receive the standard invalid-stream `TypeError`.

Scheme recognition is narrower than a general URI parser. Lowercase `data:` is
the only no-slashes special form. Otherwise a scheme needs `://`, more than one
character and only ASCII letters, digits, plus, minus or dot. Registered wrapper
lookup is case-insensitive: `file`, `php` and `glob` are local, while `data`,
`http` and `ftp` are not. An unknown syntactically valid wrapper emits the exact
warning and is treated as local; an invalid or one-character scheme is simply a
local path.

Resource locality follows wrapper metadata: plain files are local and RFC2397
streams are not. Wrapper/resource creation is unchanged and remains a separate
capability.

TTY status is exactly whether `TCGETS` succeeds on the underlying file
descriptor. RFC2397 streams and regular files return false; `/dev/ptmx` provides
a stable true-path oracle on this Linux-linked build. The leaf exposes no
termios fields and performs no terminal mutation.

The differential exposed an existing interpreter mismatch in strict
`in_array()` for string needles (`rfc2397` was not found in a literal string
array). The new locality body uses three direct comparisons rather than relying
on that wrong native path; this unit did not widen into an unrelated array fix.

As with the preceding stream units, php-src owns the resource capability under
`main/streams` and exposes these functions from `ext/standard/streamsfuncs.c`;
there is no `ext/streams` extension.

validation still owns null deprecation, scalar coercion, array/object errors,

## 2026-08-30 -- modeled peak-memory reset became a PHP no-op

### Work summary

models `memory_get_usage()` and `memory_get_peak_usage()` as the same fixed

still runs after the public engine signature validates the call.

### Findings

The linked function takes no arguments, returns `null` through its `void`
signature and rejects any extra argument with the exact public
`ArgumentCountError`. A real reset makes the subsequent peak no greater than
the previous peak and at least the current usage. It need not make the two

observable post-reset invariants.

## 2026-08-30 -- filesystem predicates gained one loader-aware status leaf

### Work summary

Moved `file_exists()`, `is_dir()`, `is_executable()`, `is_file()`,
`is_link()`, `is_readable()`, `is_writable()` and `is_writeable()` into the
harvested standard library. The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 140
userland and 177 pending**: `file_exists()` left the native dispatcher and the
other seven left pending.

One narrow runtime primitive now reports existence, file/directory/link type
and read/write/execute access. The optional loader inspector answers for its
owned namespace; the embedded implementation treats indexed sources as
readable immutable non-executable files and path-derived directories as
readable/searchable immutable directories. Absolute paths outside `/app`
still fall through to direct host inspection. No full stat shape, mutation,
directory handle, stream resource or wrapper lifecycle was added.

### Findings

`file_exists()` and all type/access predicates except `is_link()` follow
symlinks. `is_link()` uses link identity itself and therefore remains true for
a broken link, while existence and target predicates are false. Executability
is a POSIX access check and applies to searchable directories as well as
regular files; readability and writability likewise use the process's real
access rather than only mode-bit inference.

These eight functions deliberately return false for NUL-bearing paths instead
of raising the path `ValueError` used by many other file functions. `file://`
and case-insensitive localhost file URIs share plain-file behavior; registered
non-file wrappers return false silently, while an unknown syntactically valid
wrapper emits the public function's exact warning. PHP bodies retain manifest
coercions, null deprecation, named arguments and type/arity errors, including
the historical `is_writeable()` spelling in diagnostics.

## 2026-08-30 -- include-path resolution gained one loader-aware leaf

### Work summary

Moved `stream_resolve_include_path()` into the harvested stream library. The
549-function ledger is now **233 native, 132 userland and 184 pending**.

One narrow runtime primitive was added: canonical path resolution against the
installed loader or the host fallback. The embedded loader recognizes both
indexed files and directories derived from their paths, blocks virtual-root
escapes, and explicitly defers absolute paths outside `/app` to the host. It
does not open a stream or add wrapper, context, filter, socket or directory
resource capabilities.

### Findings

Relative names search `include_path` in order, then fall back to the executing
script's directory; they do not implicitly search the process working directory
while a nonempty search path is present. Empty path elements have PHP's literal
Unix behavior, and `file://` entries must be split without treating their scheme
colon as `PATH_SEPARATOR`. Successful file, directory and symlink lookups return
canonical paths.

The linked wrapper registry is the fixed set `php`, `file`, `glob`, `data`,
`http` and `ftp`. Only the plain-file wrapper can resolve here; known non-file
wrappers return false, while a syntactically valid unknown scheme emits the
engine's exact warning. The PHP body retains path-NUL validation and uses a
hidden `mixed` parameter so public manifest coercions, null deprecation, named
arguments and type/arity errors remain internal-function behavior.

## 2026-08-30 -- multisort was a stable permutation over existing array facts

### Work summary

Moved `array_multisort()` into the harvested standard library. The
549-function ledger is now **233 native, 116 userland and 200 pending**.

No new runtime primitive was added. PHP parses the interleaved array/order/type
grammar, builds one stable lexicographic permutation through existing
`usort()`, and applies it to every referenced column. Existing
`PHP2Go\Internal\array_id()` deduplicates aliased columns before mutation.

### Findings

Each array begins with `SORT_ASC | SORT_REGULAR` defaults and accepts at most
one order and one type flag before the next array. Non-integer non-arrays raise
`TypeError`; unknown integer flags raise `ValueError`; a repeated valid flag
raises the distinct “not already specified” `TypeError`. Size consistency is
checked before comparisons or mutation.

The case bit is accepted with every comparison base but affects only string and
natural modes. Regular mode uses PHP comparison, numeric mode deliberately
converts through float, and string/natural modes use their existing byte
comparators. The float conversion is observable at `PHP_INT_MAX`: adjacent
64-bit integers collapse to equal and stability preserves their input order.
Locale-string order is byte-string order in the only currently reachable C
locale; adding `setlocale()` later must route this branch through that future
locale contract.

String keys survive while numeric keys are renumbered. Reordering by key rank
with `uksort()`, followed by one-array `array_merge()`, preserves bucket
references. The differential exposed that php2go's native `array_merge()`
was dereferencing every element; it now iterates raw buckets and uses the
existing `php.CopyElement` rule, matching Zend for shared references.

### Verification

- linked-engine probes covered every sort mode and case-bit combination,
  interleaved flags, repeated/invalid flags, inconsistent sizes, mixed keys,
  multiple columns, aliases, references, temporaries, stability, large numeric
  precision and comparison exceptions

  public composite in a generated bundle

## 2026-08-30 -- meta tags needed a lexer, not a tokenizer capability

### Work summary

Moved `get_meta_tags()` into the harvested standard library. The
549-function ledger is now **233 native, 115 userland and 201 pending**.

No new runtime primitive was added. The PHP body ports the function's small
HTML-token grammar over the existing diagnostic-free
`PHP2Go\Internal\read_file()` leaf, so embedded assets, include-path
candidates, RFC2397 data and host files share the same source boundary.

### Findings

The linked engine does not use an HTML parser here. Its scanner emits only
open/close tags, slash, equals, literal space, HTML-4 identifier, quoted-string
and other tokens. Newline, carriage return and tab are skipped; comments and
`<body>` have no special meaning. Parsing stops only when a slash/head token
pair is seen inside a tag.

A quote ends at its matching quote, `<`, `>` or the 8,192-byte token cap,
so `>` inside a quoted value closes the tag. Malformed tags recover when a
new open-tag token appears. Attribute order is irrelevant, later duplicate
names replace values without moving array order, and missing content becomes
an empty string.

Names are lowercased and only the fixed unsafe byte set
` .\\+*?[^]$()` becomes underscores; entities are not decoded. Input stops
at its first NUL byte. Empty paths, NUL paths and missing-source warnings reuse
the same validation and diagnostic contracts as the other file composites.

### Verification

  quoted/unquoted values, comments, head termination, malformed recovery,
  duplicates, numeric keys, unsafe-name normalization and token-length caps

## 2026-08-30 -- IPTC stayed a byte grammar over the existing source seam

### Work summary

Moved `iptcparse()` and `iptcembed()` into the harvested standard
library. The 549-function ledger is now **233 native, 114 userland and 202
pending**.

No new runtime primitive was added. `iptcparse()` is a PHP byte parser;
`iptcembed()` composes JPEG marker rewriting over the existing diagnostic-free
`PHP2Go\Internal\read_file()` leaf. The bundle source reader was corrected
to defer absolute paths outside `/app` to the established host-file fallback,
while malformed or escaping virtual paths remain hard errors.

### Findings

The linked engine scans leading junk for the first record 1 or 2 IPTC marker,
accepts short and extended big-endian lengths, groups repeated datasets under
keys such as `2#005`, and stops cleanly at malformed or truncated records.

Embedding inserts a Photoshop APP13 segment after the first APP0 or APP1,
replaces an existing APP13 segment and NUL-pads odd IPTC payloads. Spool modes
below 1 return bytes without output, mode 1 outputs and returns the bytes, and
modes 2 or greater output and return `true`. Invalid JPEG prefixes have
observable partial-output behavior.

High-byte strings written as constant-foldable `chr()` expressions cannot be
harvested into protobuf string constants because those constants require valid
UTF-8. Routing byte construction through a private PHP helper keeps the
expression dynamic and preserves arbitrary bytes without widening the IR.

## 2026-08-30 -- file-content composites reused the embedded byte seam

### Work summary

Moved `file()`, `readfile()`, `md5_file()` and `sha1_file()` into the
harvested standard library. The 549-function ledger is now **233 native,
112 userland and 204 pending**.

No new runtime leaf was added. All four functions use the existing
diagnostic-free `PHP2Go\Internal\read_file()` boundary, which checks the
bundle's embedded source map before falling back to host files and the RFC2397
reader. Line shaping, include-path search, output, hashes, binary digest
conversion, validation and public warnings remain PHP.

### Findings

`file()` recognizes LF as the line delimiter on this build.
`FILE_IGNORE_NEW_LINES` removes the LF and one preceding CR; a bare CR is
ordinary data. `FILE_SKIP_EMPTY_LINES` tests the resulting line, so it
only removes a blank LF line when combined with `FILE_IGNORE_NEW_LINES`.
A final LF does not manufacture a trailing empty element.
`FILE_USE_INCLUDE_PATH` searches the modeled include path first, so bundled
virtual directories participate without a resolver primitive.

`readfile()` writes exact bytes and returns their byte count. The engine
type-checks a scalar context before reading, but rejects a resource of the
wrong kind only after writing the bytes; the PHP composite preserves that
observable order. File hashes reuse in-memory `md5()` and `sha1()`, with
`hex2bin()` supplying binary mode.

The new data-wrapper cases exposed an older RFC2397 bug. Non-base64 payloads
use form-style decoding: percent escapes are decoded, an unescaped plus becomes
a space and `%2B` remains a plus. Base64 payloads are decoded raw. The
runtime now follows that engine behavior. Embedded assets are byte-readable,
but `fopen()` still cannot create a stream resource for one; that remains
a separate capability.

### Verification

- linked-engine probes covered flags, line endings, validation order,
  include-path precedence, hashes, output length, contexts and RFC2397 decoding
- `TestFileContentUserlandMatchesEngine` covers embedded assets, include
  paths, data URIs, contexts and diagnostics in a generated bundle

## 2026-08-30 -- file-like streams stopped at one payload-operation leaf

### Work summary

Moved `fflush()`, `fsync()`, `fdatasync()`, `ftruncate()`, `fstat()`,
`flock()` and `stream_supports_lock()` into the harvested streams library.
The 549-function ledger is now **233 native, 108 userland and 208 pending**.

Added one reserved `PHP2Go\Internal\stream_operation()` leaf. It exposes
only flush, sync, truncate, raw stat and advisory-lock operations on an
existing payload. Public resource diagnostics, sync warnings, the associative
stat shape, lock-operation validation and `flock()`'s optional by-reference
output remain PHP.

### Findings

Plain files and RFC2397 streams both flush successfully. Only plain files
support `fsync()` and `fdatasync()`; RFC2397 streams emit the public
`Can't fsync this stream!` warning and return `false`. Lock capability is
likewise a property of the file payload. File locks use process-scoped
`fcntl` semantics, matching the linked engine's behavior across two handles
opened by one request.

`fstat()` is a 13-value native fact vector shaped in PHP into 13 numeric and
13 named entries. The linked build exposes `rdev`, `blksize` and `blocks`
as `-1`; file identity, mode, owner, size and timestamps come from the
payload. RFC2397 streams have deterministic synthetic stat values: device 12,
regular-file mode 0666, zero identity/timestamps and their current byte length.

RFC2397 truncation is real stream state rather than an unconditional success.
Shrinking drops bytes, growth appends NULs, and the cursor is preserved even
when it lies beyond the new end. The runtime therefore rebuilds its memory
reader at the requested length without turning this operation into host I/O.

`flock()` validates the low action bits as `LOCK_SH`, `LOCK_EX` or
`LOCK_UN`, preserves the non-blocking flag, initializes the optional
would-block output to zero and returns `false` for non-lockable RFC2397
streams. `ftruncate()` checks a negative size before resolving a closed
resource, matching the engine's validation order.

### Verification

- linked-engine probes covered file and RFC2397 flush/sync/stat/truncate/lock
  behavior, stat fields, truncate growth and shrinkage, cursor preservation,
  NUL fill, operation errors and closed resources
- `TestStreamOperationsUserlandMatchesEngine` differentially covers all

## 2026-08-30 -- existing stream controls stopped at one option leaf

### Work summary

Moved nine public stream names into the harvested streams library:
`stream_set_blocking()`, `stream_set_timeout()`,
`stream_set_read_buffer()`, `stream_set_write_buffer()`,
`stream_set_chunk_size()` and their four historical aliases. The
549-function ledger is now **233 native, 101 userland and 215 pending**.

Added one reserved `PHP2Go\Internal\stream_set_option()` leaf. It is the
resource-payload boundary for blocking, timeout, buffer and chunk-size
mutation; public validation, return shaping and aliases remain PHP.
`stream_get_meta_data()` stays native because wrapper identity, mode, EOF and
seekability cannot be observed from PHP values. `socket_get_status()` is a
PHP wrapper over that canonical query.

### Findings

The linked engine's plain-file and RFC2397 streams both accept blocking changes.
They do not implement read timeouts, accept read-buffer changes with return
value `0`, reject write-buffer changes with `-1`, and keep a per-stream chunk
size whose previous value is returned (initially 8192). Chunk sizes at or below
zero and above `INT_MAX` are distinct `ValueError` cases.

Plain-file metadata has the nine `timed_out`, `blocked`, `eof`,
`wrapper_type`, `stream_type`, `mode`, `unread_bytes`, `seekable` and
`uri` fields. RFC2397 metadata instead begins with `mediatype` and `base64`
and omits the first three state fields. The runtime now retains only the
payload facts needed to reproduce those shapes for its already-supported
handles.

The next apparent pure pair, `array_rand()` / `shuffle()`, is not one clean
RNG composite. `shuffle()` can consume ranged MT output, but seeded
`array_rand()` changes its draw sequence according to deleted bucket
positions. PHP iteration cannot see those tombstones, so exposing only a
generic random-index leaf would silently lose exact behavior.

php-src has no `ext/streams` directory. The capability layer is
`main/streams`; these public functions are declared by `ext/standard`.
That split is now reflected directly: resource operations stay native and
composite public policy lives in the embedded streams PHP library.

### Verification

  state changes, both metadata shapes, aliases and chunk-size validation

  metadata query and all nine userland names in a generated bundle

## 2026-08-30 -- formatted scanning needed no new runtime leaf

### Work summary

Moved `sscanf()` and `fscanf()` into the harvested userland libraries.
The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 92 userland and 225 pending**.
Both entry points share one PHP scanner. The stream form adds exact
File-Handle validation and one existing `fgets()` call; it introduces no new
runtime primitive or host capability.

### Findings

Format validation completes before input scanning. Sequential and positional
`%n$` assignments cannot mix, an output position must be assigned exactly
once in by-reference mode, positional array mode may leave null gaps, and
suppressed fields consume input without claiming an output slot. Bad conversion
characters, unmatched character sets and argument-count mismatches are
`ValueError`s.

The scanner is byte-oriented and stops both input and format at NUL. Format
whitespace consumes the C whitespace byte set. `%s` skips leading whitespace;
`%c` and `%[...]` do not, and this implementation preserves the linked
scanner's unusual empty-string `%c` match when the next byte is whitespace.
Widths, ignored `h`/`l`/`L` size modifiers, assignment suppression,
literal percent and `%n` byte positions remain PHP grammar.

Signed integer overflow saturates at `PHP_INT_MIN`/`PHP_INT_MAX`.
Unsigned values with bit 63 set are returned as decimal strings, including
negative input converted modulo 2^64. Floating conversion rolls an incomplete
exponent back to its `e`, so a following conversion sees it. Array-return mode
preallocates null placeholders; by-reference mode leaves unmatched variables
unchanged and returns the number of conversions, including suppressed ones.
Underflow before any conversion is `null` in array mode and `-1` in
reference mode.

`fscanf()` reads exactly one line before validating the scan format. A bad
format or output count therefore still advances the stream, while EOF before a
line returns `false` and leaves references unchanged. Closed and non-resource
arguments retain `fscanf()`'s File-Handle-specific diagnostics.

### Verification

  whitespace, every integer and float conversion, widths, modifiers,
  suppression, `%n`, positional assignments, overflow, partial matches,
  underflow, NUL termination and validation errors
- stream probes covered line boundaries, blank lines, reference outputs, EOF,
  invalid handles and line consumption on errors
- `TestScanfUserlandMatchesEngine` differentially covers both public entry
  points in a generated bundle
- the affected `internal/userland`, `runtime/interp` and
  `internal/bundlebuild` suites pass
- regeneration and the surface check produced 232 native, 92 userland and 225
  pending functions

## 2026-08-30 -- binary formats stopped at two IEEE-754 bit casts

### Work summary

Moved `pack()` and `unpack()` into the harvested standard library. The
549-function ledger is now **232 native, 90 userland and 227 pending**. Their
format parsing, repeat rules, byte cursors, integer wrapping, field naming and
diagnostics share PHP helpers. `sscanf()` and `fscanf()` remain pending because
their conversion scanner is a different grammar, not a useful continuation of
the byte-format parser.

Added only two reserved representation leaves:
`PHP2Go\Internal\float_bytes()` and `bytes_float()`. They bit-cast 32- or
64-bit IEEE-754 values with native, little or big byte order. PHP derives native
integer byte order through that same contract, so no platform or stream
primitive was added.

### Findings

The linked build is 64-bit and little endian, but native-order directives remain
portable through Go's native byte order. Integer packing is low-byte truncation
after PHP integer coercion. Unpacking `Q`, `J` and `P` still returns a signed
PHP integer when bit 63 is set, while unsigned 32-bit formats remain positive.
Float directives preserve negative zero, infinities and NaN payload spelling
across native and explicit endian forms.

String formats always consume one argument, even at repeat zero. `Z` reserves
its last byte for NUL, `A` pads with spaces, and short `h`/`H` input warns then
truncates the requested nibble count rather than padding the missing bytes.
`x`, `X` and `@` are byte-position operations and consume no arguments.
Extra values warn only after the whole format is processed.

`unpack()` splits slash-delimited fields into a type, repeat and a name capped
at 200 bytes. A single named result uses the name directly; explicit repeats,
starred repeats and unnamed fields gain one-based suffixes, and later duplicate
keys replace earlier values. An explicit short numeric repeat consumes complete
items before warning about one missing item and returns `false`; a starred
repeat stops silently. The offset rebases the input, including absolute `@`
positions. `@*` is outside the string and leaves the cursor unchanged, while an
overlong `xN` reports the final one-byte read with zero bytes remaining.

### Verification

  endianness, coercions, repeat zero/star, cursors, names, duplicate keys,
  offsets, short input, overflow, unknown formats and exact warnings
- `TestPackUnpackUserlandMatchesEngine` differentially covers integer and float
  bit patterns, string/hex formats, cursor behavior, naming and diagnostics in
  a generated bundle
- the affected `internal/userland`, `runtime/interp` and
  `internal/bundlebuild` suites pass
- regeneration and the surface check produced 232 native, 90 userland and 227
  pending functions
- `GATE_TEST_COUNT=2 hack/gate.sh` completed with `GATE GREEN`



## 2026-08-30 -- the INI grammar stayed above one silent source leaf

### Work summary

Moved `parse_ini_string()` and `parse_ini_file()` into the harvested
standard library. The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 88 userland and
229 pending**. Both public functions share one PHP scanner/parser; the file form
adds only a diagnostic-free read leaf and emits its own public warning.

The bundle loader now optionally exposes checksum-validated source bytes.
`file_get_contents()` consults that source before the host filesystem, so
ordinary embedded assets and INI files use the same virtual paths as includes.
Existing engine-backed loaders and host-file fallback remain unchanged.

### Findings

The three scanner modes are policies over one grammar. Normal mode resolves
constants and `${name}` environment references, raw mode preserves those
spellings and quote bytes, and typed mode turns only lexer-recognized numeric,
boolean and null tokens into scalars. A numeric-valued constant remains a
string; concatenated numbers and negative decimals remain strings too. Bitwise
`|`, `&`, `^`, `~` and `!` use signed 32-bit results and become
strings outside typed mode.

Sections are either ignored while entries flatten into the result, or become
active arrays when section processing is enabled. A repeated section replaces
its earlier array. Offset entries create arrays, append on an empty or
false-like resolved offset, and otherwise inherit PHP's numeric-key conversion.
Later scalar and offset assignments replace one another in source order.

The input is truncated at its first NUL and an initial UTF-8 BOM is skipped.
Quoted values may span physical lines; double quotes unescape only quote,
backslash and dollar, while single quotes are raw. Semicolon comments are
scanner-state dependent, which is why raw values beginning with a quote retain
an internal semicolon but an unmatched quote does not.

`@file_get_contents()` was not a valid least leaf. PHP still invokes a user
error handler for a suppressed inner warning, producing both a
`file_get_contents()` and `parse_ini_file()` diagnostic. The reserved
`PHP2Go\Internal\read_file` leaf therefore returns bytes or `false`
silently; the PHP body owns the one observable warning. It uses `data:`,
embedded checksum-validated sources and the already-existing host read path, in
that order.

### Verification

- linked-engine probes covered all scanner modes, constants, environment
  interpolation and fallbacks, quotes, comments, typed overflow, bitwise
  expressions, sections, offsets, duplicates, BOM/NUL handling and syntax
  errors
- `TestParseIniUserlandMatchesEngine` differentially covers both public entry
  points, exact warnings, malformed input, embedded asset reads and direct
  `file_get_contents()` access to the same embedded file
- the affected `internal/bundlebuild`, `runtime/bundle` and
  `runtime/interp` suites pass
- regeneration and the surface check produced 232 native, 88 userland and 229
  pending functions
- `GATE_TEST_COUNT=2 hack/gate.sh` completed with `GATE GREEN`


## 2026-08-30 -- query registration was not an INI parser

### Work summary

Moved `parse_str()` into the harvested standard library. The 549-function
ledger is now **232 native, 86 userland and 231 pending**. No request/SAPI
primitive was added: tokenization, URL decoding, name normalization and nested
array registration remain PHP over existing string and array operations.

`parse_ini_string()` and `parse_ini_file()` were deliberately kept as the next
subunit. Their Zend INI lexer, scanner modes and constant/interpolation rules
share no useful grammar with request-query registration.

### Findings

`parse_str()` first replaces the destination with an empty array, regardless of
its old type, and returns `null`. Empty separator runs are skipped; each
nonempty `&`-delimited token splits at its first equals sign. Names and values
use form decoding, but only names become variable paths.

Registration is order-sensitive. A later scalar replaces an array, a later
nested path replaces a scalar with an array, and an empty bracket appends after
the greatest current integer key. Canonical decimal keys become integers while
`08` and `-01` remain strings. Root spaces and dots become underscores;
bracket keys are otherwise literal. A missing closing bracket flattens the
first malformed level into an underscore name, but a malformed deeper level
assigns at the last completed key.

The request parser is only partly binary-safe. A raw NUL terminates the whole
query buffer, and a decoded NUL terminates a name; decoded NULs in values are
preserved. Names created by mangling cannot smuggle `__Host-` or `__Secure-`
into a nested key, although the already-created parent array remains visible.

The linked defaults are load-bearing: `&` is the input separator, 1,000
nonempty tokens is the variable cap, and 64 bracket levels is the nesting cap.
The 1,001st token raises one public `E_WARNING` and stops; excessive nesting
removes the whole root key. These settings are not mutable in the bundled
runtime, so the PHP body models the linked defaults without broadening INI or
SAPI capability.

### Verification

- linked-engine probes covered destination reset, empty/missing values,
  decoding, numeric and append keys, scalar/array collisions, malformed paths,
  trailing path bytes, embedded NULs, prefix hardening and both input limits
- `TestParseStrUserlandMatchesEngine` differentially covers those behaviors,
  including a destination that aliases the input and the exact warning
- `go generate ./internal/userland` and the surface check produced 232 native,
  86 userland and 231 pending functions
- `GATE_TEST_COUNT=2 hack/gate.sh` completed with `GATE GREEN`


## 2026-08-30 -- shell quoting stopped before process capability

### Work summary

Moved `escapeshellarg()` and `escapeshellcmd()` into the harvested standard
library. The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 85 userland and 232
pending**. Both are pure string transforms; no process execution, shell, locale
mutation or host-I/O capability was added.

The same candidate unit included `fnmatch()`, but the linked engine exposes
neither that function nor any `FNM_*` constants. It remains pending rather than
being counted as a userland implementation that the engine manifest can never
alias.

### Findings

The linked process starts in `C.UTF-8`, and shell escaping uses that locale's
multibyte scanner before examining shell metacharacters. Invalid lead or trail
bytes disappear. Valid sequences are copied atomically, including glibc's
legacy 5- and 6-byte UTF-8 forms and four-byte values above Unicode's modern
`U+10FFFF` ceiling; overlong forms and UTF-16 surrogate encodings are rejected.
An RFC-3629-only decoder was therefore observably too narrow.

On this POSIX build, `escapeshellarg()` wraps the result in apostrophes and
expands an apostrophe to the four-byte shell sequence `'\\''`.
`escapeshellcmd()` prefixes metacharacters with backslash, except that matching
single- or double-quote pairs remain literal. Pairing is stateful: while one
quote kind is waiting for its mate, the other kind is escaped.

Both functions reject NUL through their public path-string diagnostic. The
linked `_SC_ARG_MAX` is 2,097,152 bytes: an unescaped input may be at most
2,097,149 bytes, and expansion beyond 2,097,153 output bytes earns the separate
`Escaped ... exceeds` error. These are validation policies in PHP, not a reason
to expose a shell primitive.

### Verification

- linked-engine probes covered the locale, all metacharacters, quote pairing,
  every isolated non-NUL byte, malformed and extended multibyte sequences, NUL
  diagnostics and both input/output size boundaries
- `TestShellEscapingUserlandMatchesEngine` differentially covers both public
  functions across that byte and multibyte corpus without executing a command
- `fnmatch()` was called on the linked engine and produced `Call to undefined
  function fnmatch()`; all four documented `FNM_*` constants are absent

  85 userland and 232 pending functions
- `GATE_TEST_COUNT=2 hack/gate.sh` completed with `GATE GREEN`


## 2026-08-30 -- CSV was one byte grammar over two stream leaves

### Work summary

Moved `str_getcsv()`, `fgetcsv()` and `fputcsv()` into the harvested streams
library. The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 83 userland and 234
pending**. No native capability was added: string parsing is pure PHP, record
reads use the existing one-byte `fread()` leaf, and writes use one `fwrite()`.

The three public aliases share validation, escape handling, quoting and parsing
helpers. The bundled differential exercises both the string and stream entry
points rather than treating their common grammar as three independent
implementations.

### Findings

CSV records are byte-oriented policy above an already-valid stream. A blank
record becomes `[null]`, while a trailing separator adds an empty string.
Leading C whitespace is discarded only when it precedes an enclosure. After a
closing enclosure, bytes up to the next separator are retained; doubled
enclosures collapse to one, but the configured escape byte itself remains in
the result.

For `fgetcsv()`, only the first physical read honors `$length`. An open quoted
field pulls subsequent physical lines without that cap, retaining their line
endings in the field. EOF before any byte returns `false`; EOF inside an
unterminated enclosure returns the accumulated final field. Re-reading the
whole accumulated record through the shared parser reproduces this without a
new stream-record primitive.

`fputcsv()` encloses fields containing the separator, enclosure, active escape,
CR, LF, tab or space. It doubles only enclosure bytes that were not immediately
escaped, preserves the escape byte, appends the caller's exact EOL and exposes
the single underlying write result. Omitted `$escape` emits PHP 8.4's
`E_DEPRECATED`; explicit empty escape disables escape semantics. Enclosure
recognition wins when the enclosure and escape bytes coincide.

### Verification

- linked-engine probes covered blank and unterminated records, leading
  whitespace, doubled/escaped enclosures, post-enclosure bytes, multiline
  fields, bounded initial reads, EOF, validation, diagnostics and writer
  coercions/quoting

  functions, coincident enclosure/escape bytes, closed/scalar streams and exact
  return/output behavior
- `go generate ./internal/userland` and the surface check produced 232 native,
  83 userland and 234 pending functions
- `GATE_TEST_COUNT=2 hack/gate.sh` completed with `GATE GREEN`


## 2026-08-30 -- stream records stayed above the resource boundary

### Work summary

Moved `stream_get_line()` into the harvested streams library. The 549-function
ledger is now **232 native, 80 userland and 237 pending**. No stream capability
was added: the body composes exact resource validation and the existing native
`fread()` primitive.

The shared validator used by formatted stream writes was also corrected for
ordinary non-resources. It now preserves the public function name and argument
type while retaining the distinct closed-resource diagnostic.

### Findings

A record read is policy over an already-valid stream, not ownership of the
stream. Length zero means unbounded; positive length is an exact byte cap.
A nonempty ending is consumed and excluded from the result. An ending at the
current position therefore returns an empty string, while EOF before any byte
returns `false`.

Length boundaries deliberately do not preserve partial delimiter state across
calls. Reading four bytes from `abcENDdef` with ending `END` returns
`abcE`; the next call starts from `N` and returns `NDde`. A one-byte
`fread()` loop reproduces that behavior directly, including binary endings and
the stream's existing EOF state.

Closed resources are an awkward PHP boundary: `is_resource()` is false and
`get_debug_type()` says `resource (closed)`, but stream functions report
`supplied resource is not a valid stream resource` rather than an argument
type error. Scalars do receive the ordinary public
`Argument #1 ($stream) must be of type resource` TypeError. The userland
validator has to distinguish those cases before asking for the resource type.

### Verification

  immediate endings, endings split by a length boundary, empty input, EOF,
  negative length, scalar arguments and closed resources

## 2026-08-30 -- user-comparator sets needed an observable sorting leaf

### Work summary

Moved all ten user-comparator difference/intersection functions into the
harvested PHP library: `array_diff_uassoc()`, `array_diff_ukey()`,
`array_intersect_uassoc()`, `array_intersect_ukey()`, `array_udiff()`,
`array_udiff_assoc()`, `array_udiff_uassoc()`, `array_uintersect()`,
`array_uintersect_assoc()` and `array_uintersect_uassoc()`. The 549-function
ledger is now **232 native, 79 userland and 238 pending**.

The least native surface was two reserved callback leaves: exact callback
validation for the broad variadic signatures, and an unstable associated sort
using Zend's comparator order. Direct key lookup, sorted merge, duplicate
handling, result filtering and legacy comparator compatibility remain PHP.

The same sorter now backs native `usort()`, `uasort()` and `uksort()`,
replacing Go's observably different stable sorter. Those public sorts retain
Zend's stable original-position fallback.

### Findings

Comparator order is behavior, not an implementation detail. Zend uses dedicated
two-to-five element networks, insertion sort through 16 elements, quicksort
above 16 and median-of-five pivot selection above 1,024. A user callback can log
or throw at any comparison, so matching only the final array was insufficient.
The exact algorithm was ported once and is shared by stable public sorts and the
unstable extension leaf.

Eight functions sort every operand before a pointer merge. Normal diff/intersect
sorts values through the data callback; the ukey/uassoc forms sort keys through
the key callback. The two `*_assoc` functions with only a user data callback
do no sorting at all: they preserve the first array's traversal, look up the
exact key in each other operand and call the comparator only for a present key.
The PHP bodies begin with a copy of the first array and remove entries, which
preserves its key order and explicit references.

The old boolean-comparator convention is special. A boolean result raises one
`E_DEPRECATED` per public operation; `true` means greater, while `false`
causes one reversed callback and negates its normalized integer result. Both
callbacks in a uassoc operation share that one-shot diagnostic state. The
direct assoc data comparator instead performs ordinary integer conversion and
does not use the boolean compatibility wrapper.

php-src's reflection stubs deliberately expose `array $array, ...$rest`, while
the C parameter parser requires one or two trailing callbacks. The runtime now
uses the parser minima for arity, and the reserved validation leaf preserves the
public function name, callback position and detailed callable reason before PHP
checks the intervening operands are arrays.

### Verification

- linked-engine probes fixed callback roles and exact call order for all ten
  functions, including duplicate values, mixed integer/string keys and values,
  one-array forms, invalid callbacks and non-array operands
- the generated-bundle differential compares all ten results and callback logs,
  32 deterministic collision-heavy three-array fixtures, explicit references,
  boolean returns, by-reference callback warnings, exceptions and diagnostics

  checksum covers its median-of-five path
- the direct interpreter differential covers the repaired stable user-sort
  order and boolean-return deprecation

  79 userland and 238 pending functions
- focused Go and Bazel userland, bundle and interpreter suites pass

  `go test ./...` pass with the required CGO environment

## 2026-08-30 -- recursive walking composed around an exact leaf primitive

### Work summary

Moved `array_walk_recursive()` into the harvested PHP library. The 549-function
ledger is now **232 native, 69 userland and 248 pending**. No new reserved
primitive was added: the PHP body reuses `PHP2Go\\Internal\\array_id()` for
active recursion and the existing native `array_walk()` for exact callback
invocation.

The new differential exposed pre-existing `array_walk()` gaps, so its native
implementation was corrected at the same boundary. Array-element unset now also
releases an explicit reference binding, and an internal callback box collapses
after the callback unless a program reference escaped.

### Findings

`array_walk_recursive()` recurses only into arrays. Objects are accepted as the
root container and their properties are walked, but an object found as a value
is a leaf. Private and protected root properties reach the callback under their
raw NUL-mangled keys, and writes through the callback retain typed-property
constraints. A third userdata argument is observably different when omitted:
the callback receives two arguments when absent and three even when the supplied
value is null.

A native `array_walk()` over each container is the least callback primitive. It
owns by-reference value delivery, callback validation and the special userdata
rule: userdata is copied for every call, so a callback requesting its third
parameter by reference receives the engine warning and cannot retain a mutation.
For a leaf, the PHP body presents a one-element array whose value references the
real slot and delegates the invocation to that same primitive. The temporary
binding is explicitly unset afterwards.

Traversal uses a live hash position, not a key snapshot. A callback can delete a
future element, replace a future value or append a new element; the walk skips,
reloads or visits those slots in insertion order. It can also replace the whole
by-reference container, in which case a scalar replacement raises `TypeError:
Iterated value is no longer an array or object`. The old native implementation
snapshotted keys, recreated deleted slots as undefined, ignored appended slots
and missed whole-container replacement.

Recursion protection starts only when descending into an array, not on the root.
Consequently a root that references itself visits preceding root leaves once,
descends, visits them once more and then raises `Error: Recursion detected` at
the repeated nested array. Active identities are removed on return, so two
branches may share and visit the same nested array sequentially.

The reference cleanup is also observable outside this function. Removing an
array element that was explicitly bound with `=&` must decrement that binding,
and the writable box `array_walk()` creates must disappear when no callback
reference escaped. If a callback does retain `&$value`, the box remains and
later writes through the escaped name still update the element.

### Verification

- linked-engine probes covered nested arrays, object leaves and roots, private
  and protected keys, by-reference leaf mutation, shared references, omitted
  versus null userdata, userdata-by-reference warnings, active recursion,
  iterator mutation, whole-container replacement and callback exceptions
- the generated-bundle differential asserts all of those behaviors and partial
  state after errors
- the direct interpreter differential now covers live `array_walk()` mutation,
  mangled object keys, scalar replacement, reference-unset cleanup and escaped
  callback references
- `go generate ./internal/userland` and the surface check produced 232 native,
  69 userland and 248 pending functions
- focused Go and Bazel userland, bundle, interpreter and PHP runtime suites pass
- `gofmt -l`, `git diff --check`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and
  `go test ./...` pass with the required CGO environment

## 2026-08-30 -- inet conversion followed the linked build, not the headers

### Work summary

Moved `inet_pton()` and `inet_ntop()` into the harvested PHP library. The
549-function ledger is now **232 native, 68 userland and 249 pending**. No
runtime primitive was added: the functions reuse the strict dotted-decimal
parser already factored for `ip2long()` and ordinary byte operations.

### Findings

The linked Zend engine was decisive here. Although php-src contains IPv6 code,
this build rejects `::`, `::1`, full IPv6, IPv4-mapped IPv6 and zone-qualified
addresses in `inet_pton()`; `inet_ntop()` likewise returns `false` for every
16-byte input. It accepts only four-byte IPv4. Implementing a general IPv6
codec from the source would therefore have made php2go less compatible with the
engine it embeds.

The accepted IPv4 grammar is the same strict four-part decimal grammar already
probed for `ip2long()`: no abbreviated forms, leading zeroes, signs, surrounding
space or out-of-range octets. `inet_pton()` rejects embedded NUL with a public
`ValueError`, then packs the parsed integer in network byte order.
`inet_ntop()` accepts every four-byte string, including NUL and high bytes, and
renders unsigned decimal octets; every other length returns `false`.

The first version of the differential also exposed a fixture boundary. A PHP
source literal containing `\xff` becomes a raw non-UTF-8 string constant in the
harvested IR, which cannot be encoded in a protobuf string field. Constructing
binary fixtures at runtime with `hex2bin()` tests the same behavior without
putting invalid UTF-8 in source metadata.

  representative IPv6 spellings, embedded NUL and binary lengths 0, 3, 4, 16
  and 17

## 2026-08-30 -- password metadata needed no cryptographic primitive

### Work summary

Moved four more `main` / `ext/standard` functions into the harvested PHP
library:

- `password_algos()`;
- `password_get_info()`;
- `password_needs_rehash()`;
- `set_include_path()`.

The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 66 userland and 251 pending**.
No runtime primitive was added. Hash creation and verification remain native
cryptographic capabilities; registry enumeration, bcrypt metadata and rehash
decisions are string/array composites. Include-path mutation delegates to the
already-modeled `ini_set()` state after reproducing its path validation.

### Findings

The linked engine's password registry contains only bcrypt: both
`PASSWORD_DEFAULT` and `PASSWORD_BCRYPT` are the string `"2y"`, the default
cost is 12, and no Argon2 constants are defined. The PHP catalog therefore
models this build's actual registry rather than inventing algorithms from
php-src configuration branches. A build that enables another password provider
must be probed and its embedded registry body regenerated with the surface.

A bcrypt hash is recognized only when it is exactly 60 bytes and starts with
`$2y$`. Metadata always has the ordered keys `algo`, `algoName` and `options`.
Its cost parser has scanf integer behavior: it skips ASCII whitespace, accepts a
sign and decimal prefix, leaves the default cost 12 when there are no digits,
and saturates overflow at `PHP_INT_MIN` or `PHP_INT_MAX`. A small PHP parser can
preserve all of that without moving the cryptographic operation itself.

`password_needs_rehash()` accepts null, integer 0, integer 1 and string `"2y"`
as bcrypt selectors. An unknown requested algorithm returns `false`, even when
the existing hash is unknown. For bcrypt it compares the parsed old cost with
the requested cost after ordinary integer conversion. Option presence is
load-bearing: an absent `cost` means 12, while a present null converts to 0.
The first differential caught a null-coalescing implementation that erased this
distinction; `array_key_exists()` is required.

`set_include_path()` returns the previous setting and updates the same modeled
INI value read by `get_include_path()`. A NUL byte raises the public
`ValueError` before mutation, with the engine's argument name and wording.

### Verification

  valid and malformed bcrypt costs, signed values, integer overflow, accepted
  and unknown algorithm selectors, option coercion and NUL path rejection
- the generated-bundle differential covers named arguments, metadata key order,
  exact-length recognition, all probed cost forms, absent versus present-null

  atomicity
- `go generate ./internal/userland` produced 232 native, 66 userland and 251

- focused Bazel userland, bundle and interpreter suites passed

## 2026-08-31 -- token state and format diagnostics stayed above streams

### Work summary

Moved four more `main` / `ext/standard` functions into the harvested PHP
library:

- `strtok()`;
- `fprintf()` and `vfprintf()`;
- `get_include_path()`.

The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 62 userland and 255 pending**.
Tokenization and include-path lookup need no new host capability. Stream
formatting uses one narrow reserved primitive,
`PHP2Go\Internal\formatted_print()`, because the existing native formatter owns
the format language and its missing-value diagnostic depends on both the
argument representation and the number of leading public arguments. Opening,
validating and writing the stream remain PHP composites over existing
primitives.

The formatter audit also corrected `sprintf()` and `vsprintf()` themselves.
php2go had counted only values after the format string and reported the same
`ArgumentCountError` for both forms. Variadic formatting now includes its
leading format argument in required/given counts, while the array form raises
the engine's `ValueError` with singular/plural `item` wording.

### Findings

`strtok()` is a request-global byte cursor, not a split operation. A two-argument
call replaces the retained string; a one-argument call changes the delimiter set
for the next token. Delimiters are arbitrary bytes, including NUL, and leading
runs are skipped. State cleanup is observable: exhausting a string made only of
delimiters releases it, so the next one-argument call warns that both arguments
are required. Returning the last non-delimiter token, or starting with an empty
string, leaves an exhausted state allocated; later calls simply return `false`
without that warning. Static locals in the hidden PHP helper reproduce this
request lifetime, and the existing reserved warning bridge preserves `E_WARNING`
and the public caller location.

`fprintf()` and `vfprintf()` format first, attempt one stream write and return
the formatted byte length, not the number `fwrite()` reports. The two functions
share stream-resource validation but retain different missing-value errors:
`fprintf` counts the stream and format as its first two arguments, whereas
`vfprintf` describes the required number of items in its values array. The
reserved formatter therefore returns only a string and accepts an explicit
argument offset plus array/variadic diagnostic mode; it does not own the stream.

`get_include_path()` is exactly the modeled `include_path` INI value. The linked
engine's default is the empty string. Adding that setting to the runtime's INI
table makes both `ini_get('include_path')` and the PHP wrapper exact and also
matches the empty path the include resolver already used.

This reinforces the stream boundary: php-src's stream subsystem is under
`main/streams`, not `ext/streams`. Formatted writes can move into PHP because
they operate on an existing resource; wrappers, contexts, filters, readiness,
locking, sockets and crypto still require native capability contracts.

### Verification

- the proposed `strtok` state machine matched Zend across 50,000 randomized
  binary call sequences with changing delimiter sets
- fixed Zend probes covered unset/exhausted token state, empty strings, NUL
  delimiters, valid and missing format arguments, positional formats,
  string-keyed values arrays and closed stream resources
- the generated-bundle differential asserts warning level/message/caller,
  token-state cleanup, binary delimiters, named values-array arguments,
  formatter errors, written bytes, closed-stream validation and include-path
  equality
- direct formatter and INI interpreter differentials pass against the linked
  engine
- `go run ./internal/userland/cmd/surfacegen -root . -check`
- `gofmt -l` and `git diff --check` were clean
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` passed with the required
  CGO environment
- focused Bazel interpreter, userland and bundle suites passed

## 2026-08-31 -- identity was the only host fact two composites needed

### Work summary

Moved two more `main` / `ext/standard` functions into the harvested PHP
library:

- `str_ireplace()`;
- `http_build_query()`.

The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 58 userland and 259 pending**.
`str_ireplace()` needed no new runtime support. `http_build_query()` needed one
reserved fact rather than a host implementation: `PHP2Go\Internal\array_id()`
returns a stable identity for an array so the PHP body can detect only active
recursion while still allowing the same array to appear in separate branches.

Calls between hidden harvested helpers also exposed a general interpreter bug.
Late argument handling resolved ordinary application functions but not library
functions, so a helper call compiled as `SEND_VAR_EX` lost its by-reference
contract. Function-body lookup now includes hidden library helpers everywhere
the interpreter resolves deprecation metadata, parameter lists, pending callees
and callback/by-reference arguments, while public builtin aliases remain
internal functions.

### Findings

`str_ireplace()` remains a byte algorithm: lowercase the search view, find the
next ASCII-insensitive occurrence and splice the original subject. Search-array
entries are applied sequentially; an empty search still consumes its matching
replacement entry; scalar search with array replacement has its own exact
`TypeError`; subject arrays preserve keys, convert each element independently
and accumulate the by-reference replacement count.

`http_build_query()` is likewise a composite over supported PHP operations. It
recurses arrays and caller-visible object properties, skips nulls and resources,
renders backed enums through their value, rejects unbacked enums, applies a
numeric prefix only to root integer keys and selects `urlencode()` or
`rawurlencode()` for RFC 1738/3986. A null separator reads
`arg_separator.output`; an explicitly empty separator remains empty.

Two runtime details were load-bearing. The implementation reconstructs the
caller's visibility scope with a bound closure around `get_object_vars()`, so a
method sees its class's private and protected properties exactly as the native
function does. It iterates private helper arrays by reference because php2go's
ordinary value iteration eagerly copies nested arrays; preserving the nested
array pointer is necessary for recursive-array detection. The helper unsets the
iteration reference and does not mutate the caller.

`get_html_translation_table()` remains pending for a data reason, not because
PHP cannot express the algorithm. Exact behavior needs four document types,
multicodepoint HTML5 entities and legacy character-set tables. The runtime
currently has only HTML 4.01 entity-name membership for double-encode checks,
not a reusable codepoint-to-entity mapping. The smallest honest next feature is
a generated canonical entity dataset shared by `htmlentities()`,
`html_entity_decode()` and the userland translation-table builder.

The stream conclusion is unchanged and orthogonal: php-src has no `ext/streams`
directory. Resource ownership lives in `main/streams`, while many public entry
points are in `ext/standard/streamsfuncs.c`. Creation, wrappers, contexts,
filters, readiness, locking, buffering, sockets and crypto remain native;
bounded composites over an already-valid resource, such as the existing
`stream_get_contents()` and `stream_copy_to_stream()` bodies, belong in PHP.

### Verification

- `str_ireplace` matched Zend on fixed cases and 100,000 randomized binary
  cases
- `http_build_query` matched fixed encoding, separator, enum, visibility and
  numeric-object-key cases, then 50,000 randomized acyclic cases and another

## 2026-08-31 -- two 32-bit limbs kept overflow policy in PHP

### Work summary

Moved three more `main` / `ext/standard` functions into the harvested PHP
library:

- `ini_parse_quantity()`;
- `hebrev()`;
- `parse_url()`.

The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 56 userland and 261 pending**.
No new runtime primitive was required. Quantity diagnostics reuse the existing
message-only `E_WARNING` bridge; URL parsing and Hebrew visual ordering are
pure byte transformations.

### Findings

`ini_parse_quantity()` cannot use ordinary overflowing PHP multiplication:
that promotes to float and loses the engine's compatibility result. The body
instead parses an unsigned 64-bit value as two 32-bit limbs, detects range
crossings before suffix multiplication, performs modulo-`2^64` multiplication,
then interprets the resulting bits as signed. This preserves decimal and legacy
octal input, explicit binary/octal/hex prefixes, signed `PHP_INT_MIN`, suffix
multipliers and the wrapped value returned alongside an overflow warning.

Warning precedence is part of the parser. Extra suffix characters report the
backwards-compatible interpretation even if multiplication also overflowed.
Diagnostic escaping names controls and high bytes, except for one two-stage C
formatting artifact: an invalid prefix whose second byte is raw NUL first embeds
that NUL with `%c`, then the public warning's outer `%s` truncates the message
to `Invalid prefix "0`. The userland body preserves the observed truncation.

`parse_url()` is not a networking function. It separates scheme, authority,
credentials, explicit port, path, query and fragment without resolving
anything. Direct probes confirmed that negative component identifiers request
the full array, an explicit port zero is distinguishable from no port, controls
inside returned components become underscores, and component insertion order is
observable. Relative authorities, IPv6 brackets, scheme-only strings and
binary input all remain PHP parsing.

`hebrev()` first divides the byte string into Hebrew and non-Hebrew blocks,
reverses block order while mirroring paired punctuation, and then performs a
second backward line-breaking pass. Raw NUL remains data. A negative line width
takes the engine's unusual one-byte-at-a-time path rather than behaving like
unlimited width.

### Verification

- `parse_url` matched Zend for fixed component/error cases and 150,000
  randomized structured binary strings
- `hebrev` matched upstream cases and 50,000 randomized mixed-direction byte
  strings at six line widths
- `ini_parse_quantity` matched values and exact warnings for valid base/suffix
  matrices, signed and overflow boundaries, escaped binary diagnostics and more
  than 200,000 randomized inputs
- the generated-bundle differential checks caller-attributed quantity warnings,
  URL array ordering/components and Hebrew line breaking
- `go run ./internal/userland/cmd/surfacegen -root . -check`
- focused Go and Bazel userland/bundle suites passed
- `GATE_TEST_COUNT=2 hack/gate.sh` finished with `GATE GREEN`

## 2026-08-31 -- invalid UTF-8 is a cursor policy, not just replacement

### Work summary

Moved three more `main` / `ext/standard` functions into the harvested PHP
library:

- `metaphone()`;
- `utf8_encode()`;
- `utf8_decode()`.

The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 53 userland and 264 pending**.
No new runtime primitive was needed. The deprecated UTF-8 functions reuse the
existing message-only `E_DEPRECATED` bridge, while conversion and metaphone
remain PHP byte algorithms.

### Findings

`utf8_encode()` is the direct ISO-8859-1 mapping: ASCII remains one byte and
each high byte becomes one two-byte UTF-8 sequence. `utf8_decode()` has a more
important cursor contract. An invalid sequence produces one question mark for
the span the scanner rejects. If the offending byte can begin a valid character,
the scanner leaves it for the next iteration; otherwise it consumes that byte as
part of the malformed span. Valid code points above 255 also become a single
question mark. Replacing every invalid byte independently would therefore
diverge on truncated and interrupted sequences.

Both UTF-8 functions diagnose every call, including empty input, as
`E_DEPRECATED` with the PHP 8.2 migration message. The internal diagnostic
bridge preserves that engine level and reports the public `main.php` call site
rather than the hidden library frame.

Metaphone is likewise byte-oriented. It skips nonletters, stops at a raw NUL,
has special handling for the first phoneme and applies digraph rules while
advancing the input cursor. Its maximum is checked between source letters, not
after every emitted byte: an `X` iteration appends `KS`, so
`metaphone('AX', 2)` is `AKS`. Truncating the result to the requested length
would erase this engine-observed edge.

### Verification

- direct Zend comparisons completed with zero mismatches for 50,000 randomized
  byte strings at six metaphone caps, fixed upstream phrases and raw-NUL cases
- UTF-8 comparisons covered the complete Latin-1 encoder domain, all 65,536
  two-byte decoder inputs and 100,000 randomized byte strings with zero
  mismatches
- the generated-bundle differential checks exact deprecation level, message,
  caller filename and line, plus malformed UTF-8 and metaphone cap behavior
- `go run ./internal/userland/cmd/surfacegen -root . -check`
- focused Go and Bazel userland/bundle suites passed
- `GATE_TEST_COUNT=2 hack/gate.sh` finished with `GATE GREEN`

## 2026-08-31 -- one warning primitive unlocked three parsers and fixed the oracle

### Work summary

Moved four more `main` / `ext/standard` functions into the harvested PHP
library:

- `addcslashes()`;
- `convert_uuencode()` and `convert_uudecode()`;
- `version_compare()`.

The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 50 userland and 267 pending**.
The generated-bundle differential covers all input lengths through 256 bytes
for UU encoding and native round trips; valid and malformed character ranges;
binary escaping; malformed, truncated and permissively decoded UU input; the
version cross product, every supported operator and invalid operators. Warning
checks additionally assert the exact level, message, public filename and line.

### Findings

These functions need no host capability. Their only irreducible behavior is an
ordinary engine `E_WARNING`, so a message-only reserved primitive is sufficient:
range parsing and UU validation remain PHP. The primitive recovers the public
call site by walking past hidden library frames; otherwise correct warnings
would expose `.php2go` implementation paths.

`addcslashes()` builds a 256-byte character mask. Ranges must ascend, malformed
ranges can emit more than one warning, named controls use their C escapes and
other selected control or high bytes use three-digit octal. Empty input returns
before parsing the character list, so even an invalid list produces no warning.

UU encoding uses 45-byte lines, a backtick for zero sextets and a final
backtick line. Decoding is intentionally permissive: encoded characters are
reduced with `(ord($byte) - 32) & 63`, while structurally invalid or empty input
warns and returns `false`.

Version comparison is a byte parser, not a dependency on a package manager.
It truncates at raw NUL, canonicalizes separators and ranks `dev`, alpha, beta,
RC, numeric and patch forms. Direct probes also exposed a current Zend edge:
a nonempty value canonicalized to no components retains an asymmetric scanner
result, so even `version_compare('.', '.')` returns `-1`; the replacement
preserves that behavior rather than normalizing it away.

The linked Zend oracle had also been leaving
`PG(during_request_startup)` set because it evaluates strings directly instead
of entering through `php_execute_script()`. Consequently `php_error_docref()`
misnamed ordinary function warnings as `PHP Request Startup`. The oracle now
makes the same execution-phase transition as the normal engine path, with a
focused regression for the public `addcslashes()` warning.

### Verification

- direct proposed-body comparisons against Zend completed with zero mismatches
  over exhaustive representative byte, range and version matrices

## 2026-08-31 -- byte algorithms exposed lookahead, not host capability

### Work summary

Moved five more `main` / `ext/standard` functions into the harvested PHP
library:

- `quoted_printable_encode()`;
- `soundex()`;
- `str_increment()` and `str_decrement()`;
- `stripcslashes()`.

The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 46 userland and 271 pending**.
The generated-bundle differential covers every input byte for quoted-printable
encoding, encode/decode round trips, raw-NUL and soft-break decoder edges,
Soundex separators, alphanumeric carry and borrow, validation and underflow
errors, and hexadecimal/octal/C-style escapes.

### Findings

Quoted-printable encoding is not a generic greedy 75-column wrapper. Encoded
ASCII folds only after its three-byte token crosses the payload limit, while
bytes `0x80..0xdf`, `0xe0..0xef` and `0xf0..0xf4` reserve space for one, two or
three following encoded bytes. An exhaustive `0x00..0xff` comparison caught
the variable-width lines that simple repeated-NUL and ASCII cases missed.
Tabs are always encoded, CRLF is the only hard line ending preserved by the
encoder, and a space immediately before CR is encoded.

Auditing the paired decoder found two gaps in its earlier userland body. A raw
NUL in encoded input terminates current Zend decoding, and `=` followed by
optional spaces/tabs and EOF, lone CR, lone LF or CRLF is a soft break. The
body now matches those behaviors as well as hexadecimal and malformed escapes.

Soundex ignores non-ASCII and punctuation bytes without changing duplicate
suppression; ASCII vowels plus `H`, `W` and `Y` reset it. String increment and
decrement operate on ASCII alphanumeric classes independently. Borrow removes
a newly produced leading zero from a multi-character value (`10a` becomes
`9z`), but `1` becomes `0`; any input already beginning with zero is outside
the decrement range. `stripcslashes()` needs only byte iteration, two-digit
hexadecimal parsing, three-digit octal parsing and the seven named C escapes.

### Verification

- direct proposed-body comparisons against Zend completed with zero mismatches
  over exhaustive representative byte and alphanumeric sweeps
- `go run ./internal/userland/cmd/surfacegen -root . -check`
- focused Go and Bazel interpreter/userland/bundle suites passed

## 2026-08-31 -- base conversion needed one diagnostic primitive, not native arithmetic

### Work summary

Moved ten more `main` / `ext/standard` functions into the harvested PHP
library:

- byte counting and spans: `count_chars()`, `strspn()`, `strcspn()`;
- signed decimal formatting: `decbin()`, `decoct()`, `dechex()`;
- input/base conversion: `bindec()`, `octdec()`, `hexdec()`,
  `base_convert()`.

The 549-function ledger is now **232 native, 36 userland and 281 pending**.
Generated-bundle coverage includes binary bytes, all compact count modes,
invalid-mode errors, negative and out-of-range span slices, signed 64-bit
formatting, ignored invalid digits, E_DEPRECATED level/message, integer and
floating overflow paths, large-base output and invalid-base ValueErrors.

### Findings

`strspn()` and `strcspn()` use substring-style bounds. A positive offset past
the end yields zero; a negative offset before the front clamps to the front; a
negative length removes bytes from the end. An out-of-range ValueError inferred
from other string APIs would have been wrong.

`decbin()`, `decoct()` and `dechex()` are exactly `sprintf('%b')`,
`sprintf('%o')` and `sprintf('%x')` for the full signed 64-bit range,
including two's-complement negative output. They need no conversion machinery
of their own.

The inverse functions accept optional `0b`, `0o` and `0x` prefixes, ignore
other invalid characters, and emit one internal `E_DEPRECATED`. Ordinary PHP
can raise only the observably distinct `E_USER_DEPRECATED`, so the minimal new
runtime surface is the reserved
`PHP2Go\\Internal\\deprecated(string $message): null` primitive. It carries
no parser or conversion policy.

The parser itself remains PHP. Integer arithmetic naturally promotes to float
on overflow. Encoding must then branch: integer values use `%` and
`intdiv()` to preserve exact values above 2^53, while floats use `fmod()` and
`floor()` to reproduce Zend's rounded large-number spelling. Treating every
value as a float matched one overflow case but silently changed a large integer.

missed specialized interpreter dispatchers.

The generated PHP stubs, not `PHP_FUNCTION` declarations, are the public
