## 2026-08-29 -- a frame's locals go before the exception reaches the caller

Interpreter track, round 314.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4347 | **4348** |
| failed | 210 | 209 |
| unsupported | 154 | 154 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 92.2% | **92.3%** |

Fixed: `bug52361`. Nothing newly failing. Differential cases 1063 -> 1064.

### A better way to rank

Counting only the differing lines that carry **no `%` wildcard** finds tests the
harness would already accept but for one real difference. Four tests came out at
zero real differences -- every mismatch was on a line the EXPECTF matcher covers,
so the failure was elsewhere, usually an *ordering* difference between two whole
blocks. `bug52361` was one: both stack traces were right, printed the wrong way
round.

### The rule

```php
function bbb() { $a = new aaa(); throw new Exception(__FUNCTION__); }
```

`$a` goes when `bbb`'s frame goes -- `zend_free_compiled_variables` in the leave
helper -- so `aaa::__destruct` runs *before* the exception reaches the caller's
catch. php2go only released a frame's locals when it returned normally.

Where the release goes matters three times over, and each placement was found by
a test:

- **After `ctx.PopCall()`**, not inside `runFrame`: the engine frees the CVs with
  the frame already off the stack, so the destructor's own trace shows the *call
  site* and not the callee. Inside `runFrame` it showed `bbb()` as frame #1.
- **After the constructor bookkeeping.** `new B()` whose constructor throws has
  to give up the half-built object first, or what it held stays reachable and
  the destructor runs late. That is `bug49893`.
- **Holding the in-flight exception.** No slot names it until a CATCH stores it,
  and it holds the arguments of every frame it captured, so without it as a root
  the walk frees what a trace still has a claim on.

### An exception's trace holds arguments, not the receiver

`throwableState` was not walked at all, so
`sensitive_parameter_value_keeps_object_alive` -- which reaches an object through
`$e->getTrace()[0]['args'][0]` -- had already run its destructor. Walking the
trace fixes it, and walking `frame.This` as well breaks `bug49893`: the engine's
exception trace reports the arguments and not the receiver, so `$this` of the
frame that threw is not kept alive by the exception it threw.

## 2026-08-29 -- a dynamic property can shadow a private one, and then there are two

Interpreter track, round 313.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4345 | **4347** |
| failed | 212 | 210 |
| unsupported | 154 | 154 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 92.2% | **92.2%** |

Fixed: `foreach_shadowed_dyn_property`, `property_hooks/foreach`. Nothing newly
failing. Differential cases 1062 -> 1063.

### The rule

Round 304 gave a private property its own `\0Owner\0name` key whenever another
**class** in the chain declares the name. A *dynamic* property can claim it
too, and at run time:

```php
class A { private $shadowed = 'A'; public function test() { foreach ($this as $k => $v) ... } }
#[AllowDynamicProperties] class B extends A {}
$b = new B;
$b->shadowed = 'Global';   // cannot see A's private one, so it grows its own
$b->test();                // inside A, `shadowed` is still 'A'
```

php2go had one slot and the write overwrote it. The write is now the moment the
declared one moves aside: `hideDeclaredSlot` renames it to its engine key,
`php.Array.Rekey` does that **in place** because the table's order is
observable -- unsetting and re-adding would move a property declared first to
the end.

### Three enumerations, not one

`visibleProps` had the round-304 rules; `lazyVisibleProps` (what `foreach` uses
when the class has hooks) and `hookedVisibleProps` (what `get_object_vars`
uses) did not, and each needed the same two:

- read the declared property through `propertySlot`, so the scope that owns it
  finds it under its own key;
- in the tail loop that hands out whatever the class never declared, skip a
  declared property's own key -- the loop above already answered for every one
  the class knows.

A third rule came out of the differential case rather than the corpus: **a
dynamic property is public**, whatever the class declares under that name --
and it may well declare a private one, since that is what let the dynamic
property exist. All three enumerations were asking `propVisible`, which looks at
the *declaration*, and so hid it.

### Traps

- **`hooks.go` has three functions with near-identical tails.** Two `python`
  replacements went into the wrong one and compiled -- the second only failed
  because it referenced a variable that did not exist there. Count the matches
  before replacing.
- **`declared[name]` and "already answered" are different questions.** Skipping
  the tail on `declared` alone hides a dynamic property of a declared name; the
  tail now asks whether `visible` already holds the key.

## 2026-08-29 -- reflection order is declaration order, and the table is not

Interpreter track, round 312.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4344 | **4345** |
| failed | 213 | 212 |
| unsupported | 154 | 154 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 92.2% | **92.2%** |

Fixed: `lazy_objects/skipLazyInitialization`, 28 wrong lines of 195. Nothing
newly failing. Differential cases 1061 -> 1062.

### 1. A static property keeps its place

`ReflectionClass::getProperties()` lists each level's properties in
**declaration** order. php2go's property table is sorted by *slot offset*
instead -- which is what `var_dump` and `foreach` expose -- and a static
property has no slot among the instance ones, so the harvester had been sorting
statics to the end of the list:

```
engine:  prot, pubA, static, noDefault, initialized, virtual
php2go:  prot, pubA, noDefault, initialized, virtual, static
```

Both orders are needed, so the harvest now carries both: `Property.order` is the
index in `properties_info`, and `reflectableProperties` sorts each level by it
while the table keeps its offset order. Round 299 built the level structure;
this is the missing key inside a level.

### 2. The lazy writers name the declaring class

```c
"Can not use %s on static property %s::$%s", method, ZSTR_VAL(prop->ce->name)
```

`prop->ce`, not the reflector's class -- so `ReflectionClass(B::class)` refusing
A's static property says `A::$static`. The *dynamic* refusal above it is the
exception: there is no `prop` to ask, so it names `intern->ce` and php2go was
already right there.

### Traps

- **Two orderings, one list.** php2go had been deriving the reflection order
  from the table order, which works until something has no slot. The harvest
  is the place to keep both, not the consumer.
- **There are two `Property` structs in `internal/zend`.** The first edit went
  into the wrong one and compiled fine until the field was used.
- The IR golden needed regenerating again (`UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`); a new field on a
  harvested message always will.

## 2026-08-29 -- what a lazy initializer may hand back, and which slots a reset walks

Interpreter track, round 311.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4343 | **4344** |
| failed | 215 | 213 |
| unsupported | 153 | **154** |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 92.1% | **92.2%** |

Two tests left the failing set and only one became a pass: read the two
together. `lazy_objects/initializer_must_return_the_right_type` now gets far
enough to reach `new DateTime()` and reports **unsupported**, which is the
honest outcome for a gap. `reset_as_lazy_ignores_additional_props` passes.
Differential cases 1059 -> 1061.

### 1. A ghost initializer must return null

```c
if (Z_TYPE(retval) != IS_NULL) {
    zend_lazy_object_revert_init(obj, ...);
    zend_type_error("Lazy object initializer must return NULL or no value");
```

The revert matters as much as the message: the object is lazy again and the
initializer will run again. php2go ignored the return value entirely.

### 2. "No additional properties" is counted, not searched for

```c
/* zend_hash_num_elements(ce.properties_info) reports the actual number of
 * properties. ce.default_properties_count is off by the number of property
 * overrides. */
if (zend_hash_num_elements(&lazy_object->ce->properties_info)
 != zend_hash_num_elements(&real_object->ce->properties_info)) {
```

php2go walked the ancestry looking for a property *declared* below the
instance's class, which counts an **override** as an addition -- so
`class D extends B { public int $b; }` proxying a `B` was refused, and the
engine allows it. `propertyInfoCount` counts entries instead: one per name,
except that a private property is its own entry per declaring class.

Two neighbouring refusals were wrong too. A proxy factory that returns a
non-object says *Lazy proxy factory must return an instance of a class
compatible with C, null returned* rather than borrowing Closure's return-type
message, and one that returns the proxy itself says *Lazy proxy factory must
return a non-lazy object* -- an `Error`, and checked **after** compatibility,
since a proxy is trivially compatible with itself.

### 3. A reset walks the *reflected* class's slots

`ReflectionClass(A::class)->resetAsLazyGhost($b)` on an instance of
`class B extends A` defers only A's properties: B's own keep their values and
are not deferred. The engine walks A's `default_properties_count` slots, and a
subclass's are past the end.

A dynamic property is not past the end -- it has a slot in neither class, and
the reset clears it. Getting that backwards cost
`reset_as_lazy_resets_dynamic_props`, which the diff-set caught in the same
round.

### Traps

- **`failed` -> `unsupported` is not a regression.** It is what a fix looks
  like when the test's next step is a genuine gap. The pass count not moving is
  the honest report; see the outcome-counts note in TESTING.md.
- **A backtick inside a Go raw string ends it.** A PHP comment written into a
  differential case with `%d` in backticks turned the rest of the file into
  syntax errors 5000 lines away.
- **Do not `var_dump` a still-lazy object in a differential case.** The property
  count the engine prints for one is unstable -- the corpus writes it as a
  wildcard.

## 2026-08-29 -- a first-class callable of a method that does not exist

Interpreter track, round 310.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4342 | **4343** |
| failed | 216 | 215 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 92.1% | **92.1%** |

Fixed: `trampoline_closure_named_arguments`. Nothing newly failing.
Differential cases 1058 -> 1059. Off the top of the missing-output ranking
again (102 expected, 22 produced).

### The rule

`$obj->undeclared(...)` is a closure over `__call`, and php2go had it half
right: `invokeClosure` repacked the *positional* arguments into the `(name,
args)` pair the accessor expects, but the named ones never got that far.
`applyNamedArguments` resolved them against `__call`'s own two parameters and
refused with `Unknown named parameter $a`.

A trampoline takes any name, for the same reason the direct call does: the name
lands in the array, not on a parameter. Two halves:

- `applyNamedArguments` leaves the names alone when the callee is a closure with
  `forwardTo` set -- the same early return `call.forwarding` already had.
- `invokeClosureNamed` carries them to `forwardArgs`, which already knew what to
  do with them.

Reflection is a third face of the same thing. The engine does not describe the
forwarder: `new ReflectionFunction(T::fail(...))` answers with a trampoline
named `fail`, taking one `mixed ...$arguments`, required 0, variadic, static
when there is no `$this`, and no return type. Probed, then built as a synthetic
op_array.

### The handle number was the last line, and it was a keep-alive

With the signature right the test still differed on `ReflectionParameter#3`
against `#4`: php2go had allocated one object fewer. The engine's reflector
*holds* the closure it was built from, so the closure's handle is not handed to
the next `new`. php2go copied the signature out and let the closure go.

Adding `reflector.subject`, walked by the collector, fixed it. Worth separating
from the refcount family in TODO: this one is a missing **edge in the object
graph**, which php2go can fix, not a missing refcount, which it cannot.

`reflector.bound` was the tempting place to park it and would have been wrong --
`ReflectionMethod::getClosure` reads `bound` as the `$this` to bind.

### Traps

- **Three faces of one gap.** Calling, invoking through a closure, and
  reflecting all consult a different part of the trampoline, and getting two
  right leaves the test failing.
- **"Handle number differs" is not always the refcount family.** Check whether
  php2go allocated *fewer* objects than the engine before writing it off:
  fewer means something the engine keeps alive was collected.

## 2026-08-29 -- casting an object to an array is not asking for its properties

Interpreter track, round 309.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4339 | **4342** |
| failed | 219 | 216 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 92.1% | **92.1%** |

Fixed: `bug52193`, `get_mangled_object_vars`, `weakrefs/weakrefs_006`. Nothing
newly failing. Differential cases 1056 -> 1058.

### How the targets were picked

Ranking the failing set by *how much output is missing after a matching
prefix* rather than by diff size. A test that produces 31 of 91 expected lines
has one bug near the top; a test that differs on line 3 of 3 may have a hard
one. `weakrefs_006` (91 -> 31) and `bug52193` (93 -> 17) both came off the top
of that list. Worth keeping as a way to choose.

### 1. Writing over a WeakMap entry releases what it held

```php
$w[$o] = new HasDtor();
$w[$o] = 123;          // the destructor runs *here*
var_dump($w);          // and what it added to $w is already in $w
```

php2go left the destructor to shutdown, so the map printed one entry instead of
eleven. `offsetSet` and `offsetUnset` now release the displaced value.

### 2. `(array) $object` asks a different question than `get_mangled_object_vars`

The engine has two purposes for building an object's array form, and internal
classes answer them differently. Probed:

| | `(array) $o` | `get_mangled_object_vars($o)` |
|---|---|---|
| `Closure` | `[0 => $o]` -- the closure itself | `[]` |
| `ArrayObject`, `ArrayIterator` | the **storage** | `[]` |
| `Generator`, `WeakMap`, `stdClass` | `[]` | `[]` |

That is `ZEND_PROP_PURPOSE_ARRAY_CAST`. php2go used the property table for
both, so `$h = (array) $c; $h[0]()` had nothing to call.

### Traps

- **A cast and a var-dump of the same object are not the same enumeration.**
  php2go had already made this distinction for lazy objects (the cast does not
  initialize); the same split exists for the engine's own classes and cuts the
  other way.
- The remaining `weakrefs` failures are object *handle numbers* -- the refcount
  family already recorded in TODO.

## 2026-08-29 -- a resource is a handle, and eval is not a file

Interpreter track, round 308.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4338 | **4339** |
| failed | 220 | 219 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 92.0% | **92.1%** |

Fixed: `operator_unsupported_types`, which is one test and 962 wrong lines.
Nothing newly failing. Differential cases 1055 -> 1056.

### How the test was read

`operator_unsupported_types` ran 1983 expected lines against 1023 produced,
which reads like a wholesale failure. It is not: the first 1022 lines match, and
the script had ended early on `die("Value corrupted!")` -- its own check that a
compound assignment which throws leaves the variable alone. Three separate bugs
were behind the rest, each found by walking forward from the first divergence.

### 1. `strictEqual` had no case for a resource

It fell through to `return false`, so `$b = $a; $a === $b` was **false** for two
names on the same handle -- which is what the test's corruption check tripped
over. `looseEqual` had the mirror bug: it ended in `return ka == kb`, so any two
resources were `==`. Probed:

| | |
|---|---|
| `$a === $c` where `$c = $a` | true |
| `$a === $b` from two `fopen`s | false |
| `$a == (int) $a`, `$a == (string)(int) $a` | true |
| `$a == "abc"`, `$a == []`, `$a == null` | false |
| `$a < $b` | by id |

A resource is its id for comparison, except that it is never equal to an array
or an object. `compareAt` already got the ordering right, because a resource
casts to its id -- so the equality path routes through it.

### 2. eval is compiled by a different entry point than a file

`eval("1;")` answers **NULL** and `include` of a file that returns nothing
answers **1**, and the reason is in the compiler: a file's op_array ends in
`RETURN 1`, eval'd code in `RETURN null`. php2go compiled eval's argument by
writing `"<?php " + code` to a scratch file and calling the *file* compiler, so
every eval answered 1 -- and `$x = eval("return null;")` left `$x` an int, which
made the next `+=` report `int + array` instead of `null + array`.

`Engine.CompileEvalString` now calls `zend_compile_string(source, name,
ZEND_COMPILE_POSITION_AFTER_OPEN_TAG)`. The position matters: `AT_OPEN_TAG`
treats the string as being *outside* PHP, so the whole program echoes itself as
inline HTML.

php2go also mapped a null include result to 1, which hid a real `return null;`.
The compiler already says 1 where 1 is meant, so that mapping is gone; only an
op_array that never reached a `RETURN` at all still yields it.

### 3. `~` names the word "object" where the engine names the class

`Cannot perform bitwise not on stdClass`. `php.TypeName` -- the one
"Unsupported operand types" already used -- answers with the class.

### Traps

- **A test that looks wholly broken can be three lines wrong.** 962 of the 962
  missing lines were downstream of one `die()`. Compare the *prefix* before
  reading the diff as a summary.
- **php2eval cannot see this one.** Its engine is not the CLI, so it has no
  `STDOUT`; php2go implements neither `fopen` nor `tmpfile`. The two sides have
  no resource in common, so the differential case is a comment pointing at the
  `.phpt` that does cover it. Recorded in TODO with the other oracle limits.

## 2026-08-29 -- an initializer runs where the access was, and two rules with no corpus movement

Interpreter track, round 307.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4337 | **4338** |
| failed | 221 | 220 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 92.0% | **92.0%** |

Fixed: `lazy_objects/init_exception_001`. Nothing newly failing. Differential
cases 1053 -> 1055. Two of the three rules below move no test on their own; both
are settled against the engine and carry a case.

### 1. A lazy initializer runs *at* the access

The engine calls it where the state was asked for, not from inside an internal
function, so its stack frame names the line that touched the object:

```
engine:  #0 %s(%d): {closure:%s:%d}(Object(C))
php2go:  #0 [internal function]: {closure:...}(Object(C))
```

`callValueAt` already existed for exactly this -- `set_error_handler` uses it --
and the initializer had been going through plain `callValue`.

### 2. An engine array store hands out its slot

Same rule as round 303's WeakMap, one class of object wider. Probed:

```php
$o = new ArrayObject(["a" => [1]]);
$o["a"][] = 2;              // engine: the store really gains a 2
$o["n"] = 1; $o["n"]++;     // engine: 2
$r = 5; $o["ref"] = 0; $o["ref"] =& $r; $r++;   // engine: &int(6) in the dump
```

None of the three earns *Indirect modification of overloaded element*; php2go
earned it for all three and modified a copy. A userland `ArrayAccess` **does**
still earn it, and so does a subclass that writes its own `offsetGet` -- the
engine's handler calls the override, so the answer is a value like any other
accessor's. `plainArrayStore` is that distinction.

### 3. A compound assignment computes before it judges the write

Probed, and not guessable from either half alone:

| Write | Reported |
|---|---|
| `$o->prop += 1`, readonly **object** | `Unsupported operand types: stdClass + int` |
| `$o->prop += 1`, readonly **int** | `Cannot modify readonly property` |
| `$o->prop += 1`, **private** | `Cannot access private property` |
| `$o->prop += 1`, `private(set)` object | `Unsupported operand types: stdClass + int` |

So visibility is settled *before* the operation and readonly / `private(set)`
*after* it. `checkPropertyWrite` did all of it up front; it is now two halves,
and `ZEND_ASSIGN_OBJ_OP` runs the second one inside the `apply` closure that
already deferred the type check.

### Traps

- **A rule can be right and move nothing.** `readonly_containing_object` needed
  all of (2) and (3) and still fails, on an object handle number -- the refcount
  family. The differential case is what records the work, not the pass count.
- **"Overloaded" is a property of the handler, not of `ArrayAccess`.** ArrayObject
  implements the interface and is not overloaded; a subclass that overrides
  `offsetGet` is.

## 2026-08-29 -- cleanup_live_vars, once the live-range encoding was settled

Interpreter track, round 306.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4334 | **4337** |
| failed | 224 | 221 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 92.0% | **92.0%** |

Fixed: `bug29368_3`, `bug49893`, `try/try_finally_020`. Nothing newly failing.
Differential cases 1052 -> 1053.

### The encoding, first

Round 305 stopped here because `zend_live_range.var` is not an operand.
Harvested raw for `try_finally_017`:

```
live=[{Var:129 Start:1 End:27} {Var:164 Start:3 End:4} {Var:193 Start:5 End:7} ...]
oplines: FE_RESET_R -> VAR:3 ; NEW -> VAR:5 ; FE_RESET_R VAR:5 -> VAR:7
```

129, 164, 193 for slots 3, 5, 7. The low three bits are the *kind*
(`ZEND_LIVE_MASK` is 7): 129 = 128|1 = LOOP, 164 = 160|4 = NEW, 193 = 192|1 =
LOOP. The rest is the same byte offset an operand carries, so it needs
`EX_VAR_TO_NUM`, which `convertLiveRanges` was not applying while
`normalizeOperand` was. After the fix the same dump reads
`{Var:3 Kind:1} {Var:5 Kind:4} {Var:7 Kind:1} {Var:7 Kind:1}`, which is what the
oplines say. `LiveRange.kind` is now a field of its own in the IR.

### The rule

```c
if (range->start > op_num) break;
else if (op_num < range->end) {
    if (!catch_op_num || catch_op_num >= range->end) {
        /* the split range for loop vars */
        if (catch_op_num) {
            zend_op *final_op = opcodes + range->end;
            if (final_op->extended_value & ZEND_FREE_ON_RETURN
             && (final_op->opcode == ZEND_FE_FREE || final_op->opcode == ZEND_FREE)) {
                if (catch_op_num < range->end + final_op->op2.num) continue;
            }
        }
        ... free by kind ...
```

Every jump to a catch or a finally frees the temporaries whose live range covers
the throw and ends before the handler. A foreach's iterator (kind
`ZEND_LIVE_LOOP`) is one, so leaving a loop by exception lets go of what the
loop was walking *there*:

```php
function gen() { try { yield 1; } finally { echo "finally\n"; } }
try { foreach (gen() as $v) { throw new Exception; } }
catch (Exception $e) { echo "caught\n"; }
// engine: 1, finally, caught.  php2go before: 1, caught, and finally at exit.
```

The release itself happens at the top of the interpreter loop rather than inside
`raise`, which has neither the context nor the unit: `raise` clears the slots and
sets a flag, and the loop asks the collector. A destructor or a generator's
`finally` that throws there therefore throws from the handler's opline, which is
where the engine puts it.

### The two conditions that are not "is the handler inside the range"

Both cost a test before they were read properly.

- **`catch_op_num >= range->end`, not "outside the range".** A handler *before*
  the range starts does not free it.
- **The split-range guard.** A loop's range is cut in two around a `break` or a
  `return`, and the handler can sit in the gap. The opline closing the first
  piece is the free that jump emitted, and its `op2` is the distance to the
  loop's own free -- the same relative offset that decides where an exception
  out of a free is thrown (round 300). `temporary_cleaning_007` is exactly this:
  ranges `8..12` and `14..18` for the loop var, a throw at 10, a catch at 15,
  and `15 < 12 + 6` says the loop is still alive.

### Traps

- **A field named `var` in two structures is two encodings.** `zend_op.op1.var`
  goes through `EX_VAR_TO_NUM` in the harvester; `zend_live_range.var` did not,
  and carried three kind bits besides. Round 305 recorded the suspicion; the
  dump settled it in one step.
- **Three places build a frame, and only one of them was giving it the opcode
  table.** `runGlobal` and the include path did not, so `isFree` silently
  answered false for every file-level frame and the guard above never fired.
  The symptom was one test *erroring* while the failing set looked clean --
  which is why the outcome counts are load-bearing and the diff-set alone is
  not.
- **php2phpt could not list its own errored tests.** `printDiff` dereferenced a
  nil `*phpt.Test` for a test that never parsed, and the panic took the rest of
  the listing with it, so `-diff-kind errored` only ever showed the first one.
  Fixed; that is how the regression above was found.

## 2026-08-29 -- hooks are chosen by scope, and cleanup_live_vars needs an encoding first

Interpreter track, round 305.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4333 | **4334** |
| failed | 225 | 224 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 91.9% | **92.0%** |

Fixed: `property_hooks/private_override`. Nothing newly failing. Differential
cases 1051 -> 1052.

### The rule

Round 304 gave a shadowed private property its own slot and resolved accesses
by scope. A *hooked* private property cannot be resolved that way, because a
virtual one has **no slot at all** -- so `hooksFor` was still picking the
subclass's declaration for an access made inside the parent:

```php
class A {
    private $prop1;
    private $prop2 { get { ... } set { ... } }
    public function testPrivate() { $this->prop1; $this->prop2; ... }
}
class B extends A { public $prop1 { ... } public $prop2 { ... } }
(new B)->testPrivate();   // runs A's hooks, and A's prop1 has none
```

`hooksFor` now asks the same question `propertyAccess` does -- does the scope
declare its own private property of this name? -- and if so that declaration
answers, hooks or no hooks. `hookedProperty` also unmangles a key it is given,
so a shadowed slot resolves to its own class's declaration, and the recursion
guard compares against the *plain* name, which is what a hook knows its
property by.

### Tried and reverted: releasing live iterators on the way out of a frame

`bug69740` throws out of a `foreach` over a generator and expects the
generator's `finally` to run at that point. Releasing `f.iterators` when an
exception leaves a frame changed **nothing** measurable -- because the common
case is an exception caught *within* the same frame, where the frame never
returns an error. Reverted rather than left as dead code.

The engine does this with `cleanup_live_vars(execute_data, op_num, catch_op)`,
called on every jump to a catch or a finally: every temporary whose live range
covers the throw and not the target is freed there. php2go already harvests
`live_ranges`, so the mechanism is within reach -- except that
`zend_live_range.var` is the **raw** field, a byte offset with kind bits, and
`convertLiveRanges` copies it through unnormalized while operands go through
`normalizeOperand`. Settling that encoding is a probe, not a guess; see
[zend-operand-encoding](./LTM/zend-operand-encoding.md) for why. Written up in
TODO.

### Traps

- **"Which slot" and "which declaration" are different questions.** A virtual
  hooked property has no storage, so a slot-based answer cannot reach it. Round
  304's `propertySlot` was right for storage and silent here.
- **A change that measures zero is not a small win.** The frame-exit release
  looked plausible and was simply in the wrong place; the corpus said so, and
  the diff-set said so twice.

## 2026-08-29 -- a private property is a slot of its own

Interpreter track, round 304.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4323 | **4333** |
| failed | 235 | 225 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 91.7% | **91.9%** |

Fixed, all ten: `bug27798`, `bug29689`, `bug60536_001`, `bug60536_003`,
`closure_039`, `foreach_shadowed_property`, `gh20177`, `traits/bug60809`,
`traits/property008`, `update_consts_shadowed_private_prop`. Nothing newly
failing. Differential cases 1049 -> 1051.

This is the family TODO had carried as "two private properties of the same
name" since well before round 300, and round 303 wrote up the design for.

### The rule

The engine keys **every** private property `\0Owner\0name`, so a private
property never collides with anything -- not with another class's private one,
not with a protected `\0*\0name`, not with a public plain name. php2go keyed
its whole table by the plain name and mangled only on the way out, so two
declarations of one name were one slot and the ancestor's value was simply
lost.

php2go now gives a private property its own `\0Owner\0name` slot **whenever
another class in the chain declares the same name**, and leaves everything else
under the plain name. That keeps an object with no shadowing byte-identical to
what php2go always built, which is what made the change measurable in one
round.

Five pieces:

- `instantiate` collects, per name, which classes in the chain declare it, then
  keys the private ones apart. The key is the *declaring* class, not the
  ancestor whose table it turned up in: a class that redeclares nothing lists
  **both** of its ancestors' private properties under the one name, and keying
  by the ancestor made a third slot. The differential case caught that, the
  corpus did not.
- `propertySlot(object, name, scope)` -- the plain name unless the scope
  declares one of the shadowed privates. Applied at the eleven opcode sites
  that resolve a property name, one line each. It is safe to resolve there
  precisely because the name only changes when the access is *allowed* and
  non-magic: a scope that owns the private needs no diagnostic and no `__get`.
- `propertyAccess` unmangles a key it is given, and -- separately -- falls back
  to the object's own `Declared` record when the class's table lists nothing.
  A `use T` anywhere in a chain delays that chain's binding past the harvest,
  so `class Z extends Y` can have a slot its class table knows nothing about.
- `visibleProps` shows a shadowed private slot only inside its own class, under
  the plain name, and the first visible slot wins for a name two slots answer
  to. A *dynamic* property whose name merely happens to be mangled
  (`(object)["\0A\0b" => 42]`) keeps the existing behaviour -- distinguished
  by whether the object has a `Declared` entry for the key.
- `checkTraitProperties` no longer reports a conflict against another class's
  private property, which is `zend_do_traits_property_binding` deleting the
  colliding entry:

  ```c
  if ((colliding_prop->flags & ZEND_ACC_PRIVATE) && colliding_prop->ce != ce) {
      zend_hash_del(&ce->properties_info, prop_name);
  ```

### Traps

- **"Shadowed by another private" is too narrow.** `update_consts_shadowed_private_prop`
  is a private shadowed by a *protected*, and the engine keeps both. The rule is
  about the key, not about the other declaration's visibility.
- **The harvest's class tables are not uniform here.** A class that redeclares a
  private property lists only its own; a class that redeclares nothing lists all
  of its ancestors', unmangled, several under one name. Both had to be handled.
- **`get_object_vars` unmangles a declared slot and does not unmangle a dynamic
  one.** The existing comment recorded the second half ("hands back the table as
  it stands, mangling and all") from a test that only had dynamic keys.
- Two of the family are still open, both hooks-related:
  `property_hooks/dump` and `property_hooks/private_override`.

## 2026-08-29 -- a WeakMap entry is a slot, and what the private-slot family would cost

Interpreter track, round 303.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4321 | **4323** |
| failed | 237 | 235 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 91.7% | **91.7%** |

`weakrefs` 26 -> 28 of 33. Fixed: `weakrefs/gh20073`,
`weakrefs/weakmap_basic_map_behavior`. Nothing newly failing. Differential
cases 1048 -> 1049.

### The rule

A WeakMap is not an overloaded container the way a userland `ArrayAccess` is.
Its dimension handler answers with the **entry itself**, so all three of

```php
$map[$o][] = 42;      // indirect modification
$map[$o]++;           // read-modify-write
$map[$o] = &$integer; // assign by reference
```

reach the map, and none of them earns *Indirect modification of overloaded
element of WeakMap has no effect*. php2go was routing every one of them through
`offsetGet`, getting a value back, printing the notice and modifying a copy.

Harvesting settled which opcode to fix: all three go through one
`ZEND_FETCH_DIM_W`/`_RW` on the map, so one branch covers them. Two pieces:

- `weakMapSlot` hands out the entry's box on the write path, *without* the
  `Shared` mark `refAt` adds -- a by-reference `foreach` is a program `&` and
  keeps var_dump's marker, an indirect modification is not and must not.
- A `writeTarget` for the entry, so `ASSIGN_REF` **replaces** the entry with the
  box the program named instead of writing through the one it was handed. The
  entry keeps that box afterwards, which is why `$integer++` is visible through
  the map.

### Surveyed and not attempted: two private properties of the same name

Nine failing tests: `bug60536_001`, `bug60536_003`, `closure_039`,
`update_consts_shadowed_private_prop`, `traits/bug60809`, `traits/property008`,
`property_hooks/dump`, `property_hooks/private_override`, `gh20177`. The
largest addressable cluster left, and the reason it keeps being deferred is now
measured rather than guessed. Probed:

```
get_mangled_object_vars on `class P { private $x; protected $q; public $r; }`
                           `class C extends P { private $x; }`
engine:  |P|x  |*|q  r  |C|x        -- four slots, parent's first
php2go:  |C|x  |*|q  r               -- three, and the parent's value is gone
```

The engine keys **every** private property by `␀Class␀name` and every
protected one by `␀*␀name`; only public is plain. Protected mangling never
collides, so php2go's plain-name table is faithful for everything except a
private property shadowed by another private property of the same name -- where
the engine has two slots and php2go has one.

`propertyAccess` already picks the *right declaration* for the scope
(`ownPrivateProperty` is exactly that rule). What is missing is storage: both
declarations resolve to one `Props` key. Making the table hold mangled keys is
the faithful fix and touches every path that indexes `Props` by a program-level
name -- the ~13 `propertyAccess` callers plus roughly two dozen direct
`Get`/`Set` sites, `instantiate`, and the display/`(array)`/`get_object_vars`/
`serialize` side that currently mangles on the way out. Written up in TODO with
the design rather than started, because a half-applied key change leaves the
tree wrong between rounds.

### Traps

- **`refAt` and `slotAt` differ only in a mark, and the mark is user-visible.**
  `php.Shared` is what puts `&` in var_dump. A by-reference `foreach` earns it;
  `$map[$o][] = 1` does not.
- **A write fetch that hands out a box is only half an assignment target.**
  Without a `writeTarget` the box is written *through*, which is right for `[]=`
  and `++` and wrong for `=&`.

## 2026-08-29 -- a destructor makes the walk stale, and one attempt to go further was worse

Interpreter track, round 302.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4320 | **4321** |
| failed | 238 | 237 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 91.7% | **91.7%** |

Fixed: `ex_func_null_during_property_write`. Nothing newly failing.
Differential cases 1047 -> 1048. A thin round, and the interesting part is what
did not work.

### The rule that landed

`collectKind` decides what to free from a walk taken *before* any destructor
runs. A destructor that drops the last name on something else -- writing null
over a property, unsetting a global -- makes that answer stale, and php2go left
the second object for the next release point. The engine, being refcounted,
frees it during the destructor, so its destructor runs before the opline that
set off the first one has finished.

`collectKind` now takes another walk when a pass ran any destructor at all,
after the object list has been pruned so nothing is swept twice. It terminates
because a pass only repeats when it ran a destructor and a destructor runs once
per object; `maxCollectDepth` bounds the recursion anyway.

Probed order, `class Test { __destruct() { $box->value = null; } }` with
`$box->value = &$tmp`:

```
engine:  d1  d2  NULL
before:  d1  NULL  d2
after:   d1  d2  NULL
```

### The attempt that was worse

Running that extra pass **per destructor**, inside the worklist and before the
object's own handle is freed, matches the engine's model more closely: the
engine frees what a destructor released *while the destructor runs*, so the
object that ran it is freed last, and the handle the next `new` gets differs.
That fixed `gh10168/assign_prop_ref` and `assign_untyped_prop_ref` -- and broke
`assign_prop`, `assign_untyped_prop`, and both `*_with_prop_ref` variants. Net
-1, and reverted.

The reason is the same reason the whole family is hard. In `assign_prop`:

```php
var_dump($box->value = new Test);   // the ASSIGN_OBJ *result* holds the new Test
```

The engine keeps the new object alive through the assignment's result
temporary, so the destructor of the *old* value cannot free it -- it outlives
the object whose destructor nulled the property, and the free order is
`old, new`. php2go's walk sees both as garbage at the same moment and frees
`new` first. Reproducing the difference means knowing what an opline's result
still holds, which is `releaseCheckKeeping`'s job at exactly one call site and
not something the collector can recover after the fact.

Recorded in TODO with the four tests.

### Traps

- **Two tests in the same directory can want opposite orders.** `assign_prop`
  and `assign_prop_ref` differ only in `=` versus `= &`, and that decides
  whether the assignment's result keeps the new object alive.
- **A fix that matches the engine's *mechanism* is not automatically a fix.**
  The per-destructor pass is the more faithful model and measured worse; the
  cruder end-of-sweep pass is what the corpus wanted. Diff-set, not reasoning.

## 2026-08-29 -- clone shares a reference, and a type source belongs to a slot

Interpreter track, round 301.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4318 | **4320** |
| failed | 240 | 238 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 91.6% | **91.7%** |

Fixed: `type_declarations/typed_properties_094`, `fe_fetch_dtor_exception`.
Nothing newly failing. Differential cases 1044 -> 1047. Three rules, and the
first two only work together.

### 1. A typed property's constraint dies with the property

`$r =& $b->prop; unset($b); $r = "foo";` is allowed: by the time the write
happens nothing declares the slot. `zend_ref_del_type_source` runs as the
object's slots are freed, so `dropTypeSources` now runs at the free point in
`collectKind`, beside the weak-reference prune.

### 2. A type source belongs to a *slot*, not to a declaration

Doing only (1) broke `typed_properties_081`, where a `clone` happens between
the binding and the `unset`. php2go kept one source per `Class::$name`, so
freeing the original dropped the copy's claim too. `RefSource` now carries the
owning object and `DropSourceOwned` removes one claim rather than every claim
naming the same declaration -- which is what the engine's per-slot source list
does.

### 3. clone shares a property that holds a reference

Which is what makes (2) observable, and was wrong on its own. Probed:

```php
class T { public $x = 1; }
$t = new T; $r =& $t->x; $c = clone $t; $c->x = 7;
var_dump($t->x);   // engine: int(7)   php2go was: int(1)
```

`copyState` copied values. It now binds the same box when the slot holds a
reference -- but **only a program-made one**. Sharing every box php2go happens
to have made broke three tests at once: a spurious `&` in
`readonly_clone_success1`, and a copy that was not a copy in `bug27268` and
`bug68262`. `Ref.IsShared()` is the test, the same one var_dump's `&` uses.

### 4. Writing the loop variable releases what it held

`ZEND_FE_FETCH` assigns into the loop variable, and that lets go of whatever was
there. `fe_fetch_dtor_exception` puts an object with a throwing destructor in
`$v` and then writes `foreach ([1, 2] as $v)`: the destructor runs at the
*first* fetch and the body never runs. php2go ran both iterations and threw at
the end.

### Traps

- **A release-timing fix and a lifetime fix can each look like a regression
  until both are in.** (1) alone cost `typed_properties_081`; (2) alone would
  have done nothing without (3).
- **"Holds a reference" is two different questions.** php2go boxes slots for its
  own reasons -- descending into a property, fetching a variable for a write --
  and those boxes are invisible to the program. Anything that copies or dumps
  has to ask `IsShared`, not `RefHeld != nil`.
- Left alone deliberately: the `gc_collect_cycles()` **return count** family
  (`gc_016`, `gc_022`..`gc_029`, `gc_041`, `gc_053`, `bug70805*`, `bug64979`,
  `bug71266`, `bug70662` -- about 15 tests). They measure the engine's root
  buffer -- `gc_023` depends on the 10000-root threshold -- which a walk-based
  collector has no honest way to reproduce. Already in TODO.

## 2026-08-29 -- an exception out of a loop-variable free is thrown somewhere else

Interpreter track, round 300.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4312 | **4318** |
| failed | 246 | 240 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 91.5% | **91.6%** |

`try` 67 -> 71 of 74. Fixed: `try/try_finally_017`, `019`, `022`, `023`,
`try/catch_novar_2`, `temporary_cleaning_017`. Nothing newly failing.
Differential cases 1042 -> 1044.

### The rule that unblocked a year-old TODO

TODO carried "A loop's subject is not released at FE_FREE (5 tests)": adding the
release check was known to work and known to turn five `try/finally` tests from
wrong answers into *interpreter errors*, because the exception landed on a
handler inside the loop that had just been dismantled. The missing half is in
`ZEND_HANDLE_EXCEPTION`:

```c
if ((throw_op->opcode == ZEND_FREE || throw_op->opcode == ZEND_FE_FREE)
	&& throw_op->extended_value & ZEND_FREE_ON_RETURN) {
	/* exceptions thrown because of loop var destruction on return/break/...
	 * are logically thrown at the end of the foreach loop, so adjust the
	 * throw_op_num to the final loop variable FREE. */
	uint32_t new_throw_op_num = throw_op_num + throw_op->op2.opline_num;
```

A `break`, `continue` or `return` leaving a loop emits *its own* FE_FREE at the
jump site, inside whatever try the jump was written in, and marks it
`ZEND_FREE_ON_RETURN` (`1 << 0`, and it is in `extended_value`). `op2` on that
opline is a **relative** offset to the loop's own final FE_FREE. The engine
moves the throw there before looking for a handler, so the exception is caught
by whatever encloses the *loop*, not by whatever encloses the `break`.

`try_finally_017` is the whole rule in one test. Harvested:

```
  6  12  ZEND_FAST_CALL  UNUSED:15            TMP:8       -- run finally1
  7  12  ZEND_FE_FREE    VAR:7    UNUSED:11               EXT 1
  8  12  ZEND_FAST_CALL  UNUSED:24            TMP:4       -- run finally2
 18  10  ZEND_FE_FREE    VAR:7    UNUSED:-1               EXT 0
try_catch=[{Try:2 Catch:20 Finally:24 FinallyEnd:25}
           {Try:6 Catch:11 Finally:15 FinallyEnd:16}]
```

Opline 7 is inside the inner try (6..11), so a naive handler search finds
`catch1`. 7 + 11 = 18, which is outside it and inside the outer try, so the
engine finds `catch2` -- which is what the test expects.

### A second release the engine makes and php2go did not

`catch (Exception)` with no variable drops the exception immediately:

```c
if (RETURN_VALUE_USED(opline)) { ...assign... } else { OBJ_RELEASE(exception); }
```

So a `__destruct` on the exception runs *at the catch*, and what it throws takes
the place of the catch body rather than following it. `catch_novar_2` prints
neither "Unreachable catch" nor "Unreachable fallthrough"; php2go printed both
and ran the destructor at shutdown.

### Traps

- **"The release check works but breaks tests" can mean the check is right and
  something else is missing.** The old TODO recorded the symptom accurately and
  concluded the loop state needed to survive; the actual answer was that the
  exception was never supposed to be looked up at that opline.
- **`op2` on FE_FREE is relative, and only meaningful with the flag set.** The
  natural end-of-loop free has `op2` unused and `extended_value` 0.
- Reading `try_catch_array` directly settled this in one step; a throwaway
  dumper over `zend.Engine` under `.agents-workspace/tmp/` is worth rebuilding
  whenever a control-flow question comes up.

## 2026-08-29 -- an initialized proxy is followed, and reflection sees a different property list than the object does

Interpreter track, round 299.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4306 | **4312** |
| failed | 252 | 246 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 91.4% | **91.5%** |

`lazy_objects` 197 -> 199 of 223. Fixed: `lazy_objects/realize_skipped`,
`reset_as_lazy_can_reset_initialized_proxies`, `reset_as_lazy_real_instance`,
`setRawValueWithoutLazyInitialization_initialized`,
`skipLazyInitialization_initialized_object`, `init_trigger_foreach_hooks`.
Nothing newly failing. Differential cases 1040 -> 1042.

### Four rules

**1. A proxy chain is followed to its end.** `ReflectionProperty`'s three lazy
methods -- `skipLazyInitialization`, `setRawValueWithoutLazyInitialization`,
`isLazy` -- each open with the same loop:

```c
while (zend_object_is_lazy_proxy(object) && zend_lazy_object_initialized(object)) {
    object = zend_lazy_object_get_instance(object);
}
```

They ask about the object that holds the state, not about the stand-in, so
skipping on an initialized proxy is the no-op skipping on an ordinary object is.
`lazyTarget` in `lazy.go` is that loop. It is a *loop* because an instance may
itself be a proxy; `resolveLazy` was one hop too, and now recurses, which is what
the engine gets for free by re-entering the property handler.

**2. A reset happens between lazy states.** `resetAsLazyProxy` on an initialized
proxy lets go of the instance, and the instance's destructor may look back at
the stand-in. The engine shows it an ordinary `object(A)#n`, not a
`lazy proxy object(A)#n`: the old state is released before the new one is
installed. php2go now clears `object.Lazy`, runs the release check, and only
then builds the new `php.Lazy`.

**3. var_dump shows an empty slot only when there is a type to name.**

```c
if (!Z_ISUNDEF_P(val) || prop_info) { php_object_property_dump(...); }
```

`prop_info` comes from `zend_get_typed_property_info_for_slot`, so an *untyped*
property holding nothing is not printed at all -- not even as
`uninitialized()`. Normally unreachable, since an untyped property defaults to
null; a reset proxy's own table is exactly the case that reaches it.

**4. Reflection's property list is not the object's property table.** Two
differences, both in `reflectableProperties`:

- An ancestor's **private** property is not there. `hasProperty`,
  `getProperty`, `getProperties` and `ReflectionProperty::__construct` all
  apply `(pptr->flags & ZEND_ACC_PRIVATE) && pptr->ce != ce`. php2go answered
  `true` for `hasProperty("b")` on a subclass and handed back a reflector.
- The **order** is the class's own declarations first, then the nearest
  parent's, then further up. The engine iterates `ce->properties_info`, which
  inheritance appends the parent's entries to *after* the class's own were
  compiled. The property table travels the other way, by slot offset, base
  first. A trait's contribution counts as the using class's own and lands after
  the class body, since the binding is a link-time step.

### Traps

- **`declaredProperty` is not `reflectableProperty`.** The first is the
  instance lookup, which must keep finding an ancestor's private property --
  `$this->b` inside `B` still works. Only the reflection call sites take the
  filter.
- **Fixing the label is not fixing the dump.** Getting rule 2 right made the
  reset test print `object(A)#3` instead of `lazy proxy object(A)#3`, and then
  print two `uninitialized()` lines the engine does not. Rule 3 was underneath
  it.
- Still wrong, recorded in TODO: a property that *redeclares* an inherited one
  keeps the inherited slot, so php2go orders it where the slot is rather than
  where the source put it. Needs the harvest to record declaration order.

## 2026-08-29 -- a weak reference is cleared when the target is freed, not when a walk gives up on it

Interpreter track, round 298.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, `compile-error 0`):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 4304 | **4306** |
| failed | 254 | 252 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| pass rate of 4713 attempted | 91.3% | **91.4%** |

Fixed: `fibers/destructors_009`, `gc_048`. Nothing newly failing.
Differential cases 1039 -> 1040; one of the two new ones was failing before
the fix.

### The rule

`collectKind` pruned weak containers *up front*, against the reachability
answer that decided what to collect:

```go
// A weak reference does not keep its target alive, so an entry whose key
// has gone is dropped rather than being a reason to keep anything.
unit.pruneWeak(reachable)
```

The engine does not do that. `zend_weakrefs_notify` fires when the target is
**freed**, and being unreachable is not the same as being freed:

- A destructor may store `$this` somewhere reachable. The object is then
  resurrected and never freed, so every weak reference to it stands.
  `destructors_009` is exactly this, made harder to see by the destructor also
  suspending a fiber: `$ref = $this` has already run by the time
  `Fiber::suspend()` gives up the frame, so both `$weakRef->get()` checks
  answer with the object.
- Pruning is destructive. `weakRef.target = nil` cannot be put back, so
  pruning before the destructors runs cannot be corrected by the fresh walk
  `observeWeak` does when the container is read -- the answer is already gone.

Moving the prune to *after* the whole destructor sweep fixes those two and
breaks `weakrefs/gh13612`, which pins the other half of the rule: freeing an
object is also what drops what it was holding, so a destructor that runs later
in the same sweep already sees a reference to the earlier object cleared. In
that test a map is freed, which releases the handler it held, whose
`__destruct` prints `NULL` for a `WeakReference` to the map.

Both halves come out of putting the prune at the point the object is *freed* --
inside the worklist, after its destructor, before propagating to what it held:

```go
unit.pruneWeakTarget(ctx, object)
unit.freeHandles = append(unit.freeHandles, object.ID)
```

`pruneWeakTarget` re-walks and keeps the entry if the object came back
reachable. The walk is only paid when some weak container actually names the
object (`weaklyHeld`), so the common collection is unchanged.

### Traps

- **"Unreachable" and "freed" read as synonyms and are not.** Everything about
  resurrection lives in the gap between them, and php2go has no refcount to
  make the second moment obvious.
- **A destructive prune has no second chance.** php2go otherwise gets away with
  answering weak questions late (`observeWeak` re-walks on read); this is the
  one place where answering early is unrecoverable.
- **The two tests pull in opposite directions.** `destructors_009` wants the
  prune later, `gh13612` wants it earlier. Either alone is satisfied by moving
  the single call; only the per-object placement satisfies both. The diff-set
  caught the regression that the total would have hidden -- +2/-1 still reads
  as progress.

## 2026-08-29 -- yield from has three refusals, and php2go had one

Interpreter track, round 297.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,302 | **4,304** |
| failed | 256 | 254 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

`generators/` went 132 -> **134** of 153 attempted. Fixed:
`yield_from_aborted_generator_with_children`, `yield_from_already_running`.
None newly failing. Differential cases 1,022 -> 1,023.

### The three

`ZEND_YIELD_FROM` checks the delegate before it starts draining, and the two
checks it makes are *different errors* from the one php2go had:

| when | outcome |
|---|---|
| the delegate's frame is gone (`execute_data == NULL`) | `Error: Generator passed to yield from was aborted without proper return and is unable to continue` |
| the delegate is the generator currently being run | `Error: Impossible to yield from the Generator being currently run` |
| the delegate aborts *during* the delegation | `ClosedGeneratorException: Generator yielded from aborted, no return value available` |

php2go had only the third. Without the first, `yield from` a dead generator
silently produced nothing at all -- the delegate answered "no more elements" and
the opcode moved on.

**"Frame is gone" is not "failed".** A generator that returned normally has no
frame either, and `yield from` on it earns the same Error -- which reads oddly
until you notice the engine tests `execute_data == NULL` before it looks at
`retval`. Probed both ways; php2go now tests `finished || frame == nil` rather
than the `failed` flag it would have been natural to reach for.

The "currently run" case is `g.running`, which covers the generator itself and
any ancestor in the chain waiting on it -- the engine's
`zend_generator_get_current(new_gen) == generator` is the same set.

## 2026-08-29 -- a numeric string picks its own type, and catch is an assignment

Interpreter track, round 296.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,300 | **4,302** |
| failed | 258 | 256 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

`type_declarations/` went 435 -> **437** of 449 attempted. Fixed:
`union_types/type_checking_weak`, `typed_properties_108`. None newly failing.
Differential cases 1,020 -> 1,022.

### A numeric string keeps the type it parses to

Weak-mode coercion into a union tries the alternatives in a fixed order --
int, float, string, bool -- which is right for every source except a **string**:

```
function f(int|float $v) {}
f("42.0");   // float(42), not int(42)
f("42");     // int(42)
f("42.5");   // float(42.5), with no precision deprecation
f("1e3");    // float(1000)
f(" 42 ");   // int(42)
```

php2go took the first alternative in the order and turned `"42.0"` into an int,
reporting a precision deprecation for `"42.5"` on the way. The rule is only for
a string source; a float 42.0 against `int|float` stays a float because the type
already matches, and a bool against `int|float` really does take the order.

### catch is an assignment

```php
$ref =& $test->i;          // int $i
try { throw new Exception; } catch (Exception $ref) {}
// TypeError: Cannot assign Exception to reference held by property Test::$i of type int
```

`ZEND_CATCH` stored the object into its result slot without looking at what the
slot held. A variable that is a reference to a typed property is held to that
type wherever it is written, and the TypeError *replaces* the exception being
caught rather than joining it -- the catch has already consumed it.

### Checked and left alone

`variance/class_order_error` wants
`Could not check compatibility ... because class C is not available` -- the
message exists in php2go and the branch that raises it is reached only when a
class cannot be resolved. Every class the harvest carries *can* be, so this
needs a notion of "declared yet" at link time. That is the same change two
earlier attempts made (`resolveVarianceClass` without the harvest fallback,
`linkEarlyBound`), each costing 16 tests and taking errored 3 -> 15. Still not
worth it; the record in TODO stands.

## 2026-08-29 -- named arguments, finished

Interpreter track, round 295. Continues round 294, which left two of these
one line short.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,298 | **4,300** |
| failed | 260 | 258 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

`named_params/` is **32 of 32**. Fixed: `gh17216`, `references`. None newly
failing. Differential cases 1,018 -> 1,020.

### The third place op2 means a name

Round 294 fixed `SEND_*`. The array-element form goes through a *pair* of
opcodes, and the name is on the first of them:

```
ZEND_CHECK_FUNC_ARG      UNUSED  CONST("c")  -- names the parameter
ZEND_FETCH_DIM_FUNC_ARG  CV:0    CONST(2)    -- fetches $v[2], read or write
ZEND_SEND_FUNC_ARG       VAR:2   CONST("c")
```

The fetch has no idea which argument it is filling -- its `extended_value` is 1
for every named argument -- because the engine keeps the answer on the *call*:
`CHECK_FUNC_ARG` sets `ZEND_CALL_SEND_ARG_BY_REF` and the fetch reads the flag.
php2go models that with `frame.funcArg`, and was storing the name constant's
index in it. Same bug as round 294's, one opcode earlier.

### forward_static_call_array splits its array

A string key names a parameter there as much as in `call_user_func_array`, and
a positional element after one is `Cannot use positional argument after named
argument`. php2go flattened the array and lost the keys, so
`forward_static_call_array($cb, ["a" => "b", 1])` called the trampoline with two
positional arguments instead of refusing.

Note the asymmetry with the singular form, which is *not* on the
`namedVariadicCallees` list and answers `forward_static_call() does not accept
unknown named parameters`: the array form has no such refusal and simply passes
them on.

## 2026-08-29 -- a named argument is not a positional one

Interpreter track, round 294.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,298 | 4,298 |
| failed | 260 | 260 |
| unsupported | 153 | 153 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

**No net change**, and the diff-set is empty in both directions. What this round
bought is correctness the corpus barely measures: `named_params/` went 29 -> 30
of 32 while another test in the same directory that had been passing by accident
now passes on purpose. Two tests moved and cancelled out. Differential cases
1,016 -> 1,018.

### op2 is the position, except when it is the name

`ZEND_SEND_VAR_EX` and friends carry the argument's *position* in op2 -- unless
the argument is named, when op2 holds the parameter's name instead. php2go read
op2 as a position either way, so for a named argument it asked "is parameter
number `<index of the name constant>` by reference?" and, if that happened to be
true, **appended the value positionally**.

The damage is easy to miss because it depends on where the name landed in the
constant table:

```
function t(&$a = null, $b = null, &$c = null) { $a++; $c++; }
t(a: $x, b: $y);   // worked
t(b: $y, a: $x);   // Error: Named parameter $a overwrites previous argument
```

It only shows up when the callee is declared *after* the call: with the
signature known the compiler emits `SEND_REF`/`SEND_VAR` and there is nothing
to decide at run time.

`Interp.sendArgumentByRef` now resolves a const op2 by name, and the positional
by-reference branch is skipped for named arguments entirely -- both halves were
needed, and fixing only the first left every second named argument passing by
value.

### A name no parameter claims still goes to a by-reference variadic

`test2(x: $x, y: $y)` on `function test2(&...$refs)`. Those names reach
`extraNamed` rather than a position, and both the by-reference decision and the
collection into the variadic array had to learn about them: the decision falls
back to "is the last parameter a by-reference variadic?", and `ZEND_RECV_VARIADIC`
stores the slot rather than a copy, as it already did for the positional ones.

That regression was caught by the corpus, not the probe -- `named_params/
variadic` broke the moment the accidental positional path stopped firing.

### A WeakMap append

`$map[][1] = 1` is `Cannot append to WeakMap`. php2go asked `offsetGet(null)`
and reported `WeakMap key must be an object`, after an "Indirect modification"
notice that should not have been there either -- no accessor ran, so there was
nothing to modify to no effect.

### Left

`named_params/references` is one line from passing: the same named-by-reference
rule reached through an *array element*, where `ZEND_FETCH_DIM_FUNC_ARG` decides
by-reference-ness before `SEND_FUNC_ARG` names the parameter.
`weakrefs/weakmap_error_conditions` is one object *handle number* away, which is
the recorded family.

Interpreter track, round 293.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,295 | **4,298** |
| failed | 262 | 260 |
| unsupported | 154 | **153** |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `closures/closure_from_callable_error`, `nullsafe_operator/013`, and one
that came out of `unsupported` (`ErrorException::getSeverity`). None newly
failing. Differential cases 1,014 -> 1,016.

### The sweep

Round 292 found a diagnostic php2go had invented by grepping php-src for its
text. This round did that for **all 203** of them at once: extract every string
literal passed to `Raise`/`throwError`/`fatal`, take its longest run with no
`%` directive, and grep the engine's C for it.

28 came back missing, and most are false positives -- `zend_argument_type_error`
*composes* "%s(): Argument #%d ($%s) must be of type %s, %s given" at run time,
so no such literal exists. Feeding the 28 to the engine one at a time turned up
seven real divergences:

| written | php2go said | the engine says |
|---|---|---|
| `explode("", "a")` | `cannot be empty` | `must not be empty` |
| `Closure::fromCallable()` | `TypeError` | `ArgumentCountError` |
| `Closure::bind()` | `at least 1 argument` | `at least 2 arguments` |
| `Closure::bind(1, null)` | no `, int given` | `, int given` |
| `Closure::fromCallable("nope")` | **succeeded** | `Failed to create closure from callable: function "nope" not found ...` |
| `call_user_func(1)` | `Value of type int is not callable` | `... must be a valid callback, no array or string given` |
| `call_user_func([1, 2])` | `second array member ...` | `first array member is not a valid class name or object` |

`fromCallable` was the worst of them: it never validated the callable at all, so
a bad one produced a Closure that failed later somewhere else. It now asks
`callableReason` -- the same reasons `call_user_func` uses -- and words them the
engine's way. The check has to be the **quiet** form of the follow-up
resolution, or a deprecated spelling is reported twice; that regressed
`closure_from_callable_basic` until the flag was passed.

### A Throwable's constructor has a signature

`new Ex("m", "notanint")` is
`Exception::__construct(): Argument #2 ($code) must be of type int, string
given`, `1.5` converts with the precision deprecation, and `$previous` is
`?Throwable`. php2go accepted all three.

**ErrorException is not Exception.** Its signature is
`(message, code, severity, filename, line, previous)`, so `$previous` is
argument **#6** and severity defaults to `E_ERROR` rather than to zero.
Applying Exception's rule to it cost six tests before the exemption went in --
caught by the corpus, not by the probe, which is what a full run after each
change is for. The three parameters in between are now honoured, and
`getSeverity` implemented.

## 2026-08-29 -- a refusal php2go invented

Interpreter track, round 292.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,292 | **4,295** |
| failed | 265 | 262 |
| unsupported | 154 | 154 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

`lazy_objects/` went 190 -> **193** of 219 attempted. None newly failing.
Differential cases 1,013 -> 1,014.

### `Object is not lazy or already initialized`

That message does not exist in php-src. php2go raised it from
`skipLazyInitialization` and `setRawValueWithoutLazyInitialization` whenever the
object was not an uninitialized lazy one, and the engine has no such check:
`reflection_property_check_lazy_compatible` refuses a **dynamic**, **static** or
**virtual** property and nothing else.

On an ordinary object both methods work:

```
$plain = new S;
$r->getProperty('foo')->setRawValueWithoutLazyInitialization($plain, 'Y');  // writes it
$r->getProperty('dummy')->skipLazyInitialization($plain);                   // does nothing
var_dump($plain);   // foo => "Y", dummy => uninitialized(string)
```

Note that skipping on a non-lazy object does *not* write the default -- there is
no LAZY flag on the slot to clear, so there is nothing to do. The virtual
refusal was missing too and is now there.

That invented refusal was what made `clone` of a lazy object fail: the clone is
not lazy in php2go, so the raw write on it was refused. Removing the check fixed
the clone test without touching clone at all.

### Skipping twice does nothing the second time

`skipLazyInitialization` on a property that is *already* not lazy is a no-op --
it does not write the declared default over whatever the program has since put
there. A raw write does overwrite, because it was given a value.

### How the invention was caught

By asking php-src for the message text and finding it nowhere. Worth repeating
as a check: a diagnostic php2go raises should be greppable in the engine.

## 2026-08-29 -- what a ReflectionProperty says about a hooked one

Interpreter track, round 291.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,287 | **4,292** |
| failed | 265 | 265 |
| unsupported | 159 | **154** |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

All five came out of `unsupported`, not out of `failed`: they were tests php2go
ran until it reached a reflector method it did not have. `property_hooks/` went
180 -> **184** of 194 attempted. None newly failing. Differential cases
1,012 -> 1,013.

### Five methods

`isVirtual`, `hasHooks`, `hasHook`, `getHook`, `hasDefaultValue` and
`getDefaultValue`. The rules are small and worth writing down because three of
them disagree in ways that look like mistakes:

| property | isVirtual | hasHooks | hasDefaultValue | getDefaultValue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `$v { get {...} }` | 1 | 1 | **0** | NULL |
| `$p = 1` | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| `$q` (untyped, no initializer) | 0 | 0 | **1** | NULL |
| `int $t` (typed, no initializer) | 0 | 0 | 0 | NULL |
| dynamic | 0 | 0 | 0 | NULL |

A hooked property has **no** default even when the source wrote one. An untyped
property has one whether or not it was written -- null is its default. A typed
one with no initializer has none, which is the uninitialized state.

`getHook` answers a `ReflectionMethod` whose name is `$v::get` -- the name the
engine compiled the hook under, not the property's.

## 2026-08-29 -- htmlspecialchars reads its arguments

Interpreter track, round 290.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,286 | **4,287** |
| failed | 266 | 265 |
| unsupported | 159 | 159 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
