### What the parameters do

`htmlspecialchars` and `htmlentities` were `mapString(escapeHTML)` -- the string
and nothing else. Three behaviours were being dropped:

- **`$flags`** decides which quotes are encoded (`ENT_QUOTES`, `ENT_COMPAT`,
  `ENT_NOQUOTES`) and, separately, *how the single quote is spelled*: HTML 4.01
  has no `&apos;` and uses `&#039;`, every other doctype has it.
- **`$double_encode = false`** leaves an existing entity alone.

The last one is not a syntactic test. `&lt;` passes through, `&notanentity;`
does not, `&amp` (no semicolon) does not, `&#xZZ;` does not -- a *named*
reference has to be one the doctype defines. That needs the doctype's table, so
`ents_html401.txt` from the linked php-src is now a generated
`htmlEntityNames401` (252 names). `ENT_HTML5` defines some two thousand more and
php2go does not carry them, so that combination is an `UnsupportedError` rather
than a guess that would silently re-encode a real entity.

### Scope

Only two tests in `Zend/tests` touch these functions at all, so the value here
is mostly in not being wrong: `htmlentities` still encodes what
`htmlspecialchars` does and nothing more, which is right for ASCII and a gap for
anything else. That half is unchanged and still recorded in TODO.

## 2026-08-29 -- a shutdown function that stopped part-way and said nothing

Interpreter track, round 289.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,286 | 4,286 |
| failed | 268 | **266** |
| unsupported | 157 | **159** |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

**Read the four together.** One test now passes (`object_gc_in_shutdown`), one
moved from `failed` to `unsupported` (`bug71221`), and one moved from
**passed** to `unsupported` (`fibers/get-return-after-bailout`). The net on
`passed` is zero and the corpus is more honest than it was.

### The gap

`runShutdown` handled two kinds of failure -- `exit()` and a thrown exception --
and dropped everything else on the floor. Everything else is precisely this
runtime's own gaps: an unsupported opcode, the step bound, an allocation it
cannot model. A shutdown function that hit one simply stopped, and what the
test saw was *truncated output* rather than a reported gap.

Three tests were affected and all three were being classified wrongly:

| test | was | is | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object_gc_in_shutdown` | failed | **passed** | the step bound, below |
| `bug71221` | failed | unsupported | `get_defined_vars` called dynamically |
| `fibers/get-return-after-bailout` | **passed** | unsupported | needs the memory limit php2go does not model |

The last one is the reason the rule exists. Its output matched while the
runtime silently skipped the work it could not do.

### The step bound

`maxSteps` is php2go's own guard, not the engine's -- it stops an interpreter
bug from hanging a whole corpus run. It was 5,000,000 per frame, and
`object_gc_in_shutdown` allocates a million objects in one loop, which is
roughly 8M steps. It stopped at about 600,000 iterations.

Raised to 40,000,000. The cost is bounded by how long a genuinely hung frame now
takes before it gives up; php2go runs about 1.2M steps a second, so that is
around thirty seconds for a test that would otherwise never finish. No test in
the corpus reaches the bound now.

## 2026-08-29 -- two more link checks, and why the class half was already right

Interpreter track, round 288.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,284 | **4,286** |
| failed | 270 | 268 |
| unsupported | 157 | 157 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `enum/gh21760`, `inter_007`. None newly failing. Differential cases
unchanged at 1,011 -- both are compile errors, which the harness cannot ask.

### Staticness across an interface list

`class Q extends P { static function m() {} }` where `P::m` is not static was
**already** right, and for a reason worth writing down: the engine refuses it at
*compile* time, so the harvest itself fails and php2phpt reports
`compile-error`. Two interfaces disagreeing is not caught then -- interfaces are
linked when the class binds -- so `interface a extends d, c` with a static
`d::B` and a non-static `c::b` sailed through.

The diagnostic reads back-to-front, and that is not a mistake in the engine:
`zend_do_implement_interfaces` adds interfaces in order and treats each new one
as the **parent** of what is already there. So for `extends d, c` the message is
`Cannot make non static method c::B() static in class d` -- parent c, the
method under *d's* spelling, and d as the class being changed.

Only staticness is compared. A signature mismatch between two interfaces is a
larger question, and the corpus does not turn on it here.

### A trait constant that collides with an enum case

`Cannot use trait X, because X::Up conflicts with enum case Direction::Up`. It
has to be checked **before** the ordinary same-constant comparison: an enum case
is a constant with no value, so the general rule would report it as an
incompatible redefinition instead.

## 2026-08-29 -- two link checks, and a class flag the harvest was missing

Interpreter track, round 287.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,282 | **4,284** |
| failed | 272 | 270 |
| unsupported | 157 | 157 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `readonly_classes/gh9285_error`, `throwable_003`. None newly failing.
Differential cases 1,009 -> 1,011.

### Only Exception and Error may be Throwable

`zend_exception_implement` walks to the class's **root** ancestor and requires
it to be `Exception` or `Error`. php2go had the enum half of this check and not
the class half. Two things the rule is easy to get wrong:

- an **interface** may extend Throwable -- that is how a program declares its
  own throwable contract -- and only classes are checked;
- a class implementing *such an interface* is refused just the same, so the
  test is `instanceof Throwable` rather than a look at the `implements` list.

### `readonly class` needed a harvested flag

`readonly class C { use T; }` where T has a mutable property is
`Readonly class C cannot use trait with a non-readonly property T::$prop`. The
flag could not be inferred: a readonly class makes every property it *declares*
readonly, so the flattened list says nothing about the class itself, and the
trait's property is exactly the one that is not readonly. `Class.readonly` is
now harvested from `ZEND_ACC_READONLY_CLASS` (proto field 36).

`zend_do_traits_property_binding` makes **no exception for a static property**,
even though a readonly class may not declare one itself
(`Static property Foo::$bar cannot be readonly`). A first version exempted
statics on that reasoning and let `readonly class U { use WithStatic; }`
through; the engine bails on it. Reasoning from the neighbouring rule was
wrong, as usual -- the check is a plain `!(flags & ZEND_ACC_READONLY)`.

### Note

That composition is a compile error, so it cannot be a differential case: the
engine bails and takes the harness with it. The `.phpt` is the check, and the
differential case covers the half that *is* legal -- a readonly class using a
trait whose properties are themselves readonly.

## 2026-08-29 -- $this by name, and a callable that keeps its instance

Interpreter track, round 286.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,279 | **4,282** |
| failed | 275 | 272 |
| unsupported | 157 | 157 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `indirect_reference_this`, `register_shutdown_function_refcount`,
`this_reassign`. None newly failing. Differential cases 1,008 -> 1,009.

### `$this` is not a compiled variable

`$a = "this"; $$a` is the only way to reach it as one, and php2go answered
`Undefined variable $this` because it looked in the slot table. The frame holds
the instance directly, so a by-name read has to come from there.

A by-name **write** is refused -- `Error: Cannot re-assign $this` -- and the
refusal does not depend on there being a `$this` at all: the same code in a
plain function earns it. Reading and `isset()` are allowed. (`unset($$a)` is
allowed too and really does drop it; php2go keeps it, which is a corner not
worth modelling until something turns on it.)

### A stored callable keeps the instance it was lent

Round 273 settled the *scope* a keyword names at registration, because a
shutdown function outlives it. The instance is the other half of the same fact:

```php
class Test {
    function register() { register_shutdown_function('Test::method'); }
    function method() { var_dump($this); }   // prints the Test instance
}
(new Test)->register();
```

`call_user_func` lends the caller's `$this` to a callable that named an
instance method; the engine's `callable` parsing does the same, and what it
stores keeps it. php2go resolved the string at shutdown time, when there is no
caller, and got
`Non-static method Test::method() cannot be called statically`.

`Unit.settleCallable` now does both halves -- resolve the keyword, then bind
what `forwardThis` finds -- and stores the callable as `[$object, "method"]`.

## 2026-08-29 -- class constants have visibility, and a trace names the declaration

Interpreter track, round 285.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,277 | **4,279** |
| failed | 277 | 275 |
| unsupported | 157 | 157 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

1,006 -> 1,008.

### Class constant visibility was never checked

`protected const` and `private const` have been a thing since PHP 7.1 and
php2go read them out of the harvest without ever enforcing them:

```
Error: Cannot access protected constant A::FOO
Error: Cannot access private constant A::BAR
```

The rule is `staticPropAccess`'s, one member kind over: private wants the
scope to *be* the declaring class, protected wants the two in one hierarchy in
either direction. Both the `X::CONST` opcode and the `constant("X::CONST")`
builtin go through it.

**`use T` moves the constant.** A first version measured against
`declaring_class`, which for a trait constant is the trait -- so a private trait
constant became unreachable from the class that used it, and two tests that had
been passing broke (`traits/constant_001`, `enum/traits-constants`). A trait's
constant is a member of the **using** class, so that is what its visibility is
measured against. Same shape as the method rule in round 283.

### A trace names the declaration

Not the spelling the call site used, and for every kind of callee:

```
call_user_func("SPELLEDOUT")    -> #0 FILE(9): spelledOut()
$f = "SpElLeDoUt"; $f()         -> #0 FILE(10): spelledOut()
call_user_func("spelledhost::M")-> #0 FILE(11): SpelledHost::m()
call_user_func("exploDe")       -> ArgumentCountError: explode() expects ...
```

The class half was already canonical -- `traceName` reads it off the declaring
class -- and the function and method halves were not. An engine function needs
the harvested signature to answer, which the Unit cannot reach, so
`Interp.canonicalCallName` does it at the two places a dynamic call is
assembled.

### `[no active file]`

A shutdown function is called with no script location, and a diagnostic raised
by the *call itself* -- a builtin's arity check -- reports
`[no active file]:0`. Note the two spellings: `zend_error` says `Unknown` for a
file it does not have (round 275) and an exception's own `getFile()` says
`[no active file]`. Same absence, different words.

## 2026-08-29 -- a handler with no handler, and a private method that is per-class

Interpreter track, round 283.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,269 | **4,272** |
| failed | 285 | 282 |
| unsupported | 157 | 157 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `gh10695_2`, `gh10695_5`, `gh14009_005`. None newly failing.
Differential cases 1,002 -> 1,004.

### The exception handler is cleared while it runs

`ZVAL_UNDEF(&EG(user_exception_handler))` before the call. Everything about
handler chaining follows from that one line:

- a handler that throws and installed **nothing** has no handler, so the second
  exception is fatal -- which is what "exception handlers are not called twice"
  means (`gh10695_4`);
- a handler that installed one while running is answered by *that* one
  (`gh10695_5`).

php2go keeps a stack of handlers rather than a single slot, so the clearing is
a null pushed on top for the duration and removed after. The nested lookup has
to happen **with the placeholder still in place** -- dropping it first exposes
the original handler again and the two call each other forever. A version that
did exactly that hung, which is how the rule got pinned down.

A destructor's exception at end of request goes the same way: it is an ordinary
exception, the installed handler answers for it, and only one nothing handles
is fatal.

### A private method is per-class

```
class A { private function t() { echo "A::t\n"; } public function callIt() { $this->t(); } }
class B extends A { private function t() { echo "B::t\n"; } }
(new B)->callIt();   // A::t
```

`zend_std_get_method` resolves the call against the object's class, finds a
private method belonging to some other class, and then looks again for a
private method of the **calling scope** with that name. php2go stopped at the
first step and refused with
`Call to private method B::t() from scope A`.

`gh14009_005` is the same rule reached through traits -- a private trait method
used by both a parent and a child -- so the lookup has to consider what the
scope's traits gave it, not only its own table.

(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |

used to fail early and now runs to the end of its fourth section before hitting

counts together** -- failed fell by two, unsupported rose by one.

### getProperty could not see a static

Round 271 gave the `ReflectionProperty` *constructor* a lookup that includes
statics; `ReflectionClass::getProperty` still used the instance one, so
`$reflector->getProperty('prop')` on `public static $prop` threw
`Property C::$prop does not exist`. Both now go through
`Unit.reflectableProperty`.

`getValue`/`setValue` then had to answer for a static, whose value lives on the
class rather than on an instance. The write has a trap: `setValue($value)` with
one argument is deprecated and `setValue(null, $value)` is not, and the
deprecation is about the **argument count** rather than about statics. A first
version deprecated every static write and broke `bug78868`, which passes the
ignored null.

### ReflectionProperty::isLazy

A property is lazy when the object is still waiting for its initializer *and*
this property is one of the things being waited for. Three kinds never are, for
three different reasons: a **static** belongs to the class, a **virtual** hooked
property has no storage, and a **dynamic** one was written after the object was
made. `skipLazyInitialization` takes a property out of the set, which is the
same `Lazy.Skipped` mark round 271 used for the readonly a reset keeps.

`bug29368_2` and `bug43175` both want an exception thrown from a destructor to
be catchable at the statement that released the object -- a temporary passed as
an argument, or the receiver of `foobar()->unknown()`. php2go holds such objects
to the end-of-request sweep, where no `try` is in scope. Destructor timing, the
recorded family.

## 2026-08-29 -- three conversions and an include that reports twice

Interpreter track, round 281.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,265 | **4,268** |
| failed | 290 | 287 |
| unsupported | 156 | 156 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `offset_string`, `require_once_warning_to_exception`, `settype_string`.
None newly failing. Differential cases 1,000 -> 1,002.

### A failed include reports twice

Always two diagnostics, in this order:

```
Warning: require_once(does-not-exist.php): Failed to open stream: No such file or directory
Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Failed opening required 'does-not-exist.php' (include_path='')
```

php2go raised only the second, and without the `(include_path='')` clause. The
order is what `require_once_warning_to_exception` turns on: an error handler
that promotes the *first* to a throw never reaches the second, so the test sees
the stream message rather than the include one.

The optional forms end with a warning instead --
`include(): Failed opening '%s' for inclusion (include_path='%s')` -- and that
second message names `include()` whichever optional spelling was written: it
comes from a single `php_error_docref("function.include", ...)` that does not
distinguish them. The first message *does* carry the keyword as written
(`include_once(path):`), which is why both had to be built separately.

### settype() to string is the language's own conversion

An object goes through `__toString` and a class without one is an Error;
php2go used the value model's `String()`, which cannot call a method and
answered `""`. Routing it through `Interp.toString` also removed a duplicated
array warning: that function already raises it.

### A resource is never a string offset

php2go refused one for `isset()` and *cast* it for a read, on the theory that
"String offset cast occurred" covered it. It does not: a resource is refused in
every position on a string. An array is the odd container out -- there a handle
is cast to its id with a warning, which is what `resource_key` checks.

### An oracle limit worked around

The harness rewrites the function-name prefix of an engine diagnostic to
`PHP Request Startup`, so the *prefix* of an include's warning cannot be
compared in a differential case. The case added here strips both sides back to
the message body, which still checks the pair and the order; the prefixes are
covered by the `.phpt`.

## 2026-08-29 -- a __toString that throws, and where the exception goes

Interpreter track, round 280.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,261 | **4,265** |
| failed | 294 | 290 |
| unsupported | 156 | 156 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `gh10695_1`, `gh10695_7`, `gh14969`, `gh8841`. None newly failing.
Differential cases 998 -> 1,000.

### The exception wins everywhere except a return

`__toString` is a coercion, and a coercion can throw. php2go called the method,
threw the result away, and reported its own type error instead. The engine does
four different things, and the difference is not arbitrary -- it is which
diagnostic the *site* would have raised:

| site | outcome |
|---|---|
| argument (user function) | the `__toString` exception |
| argument (internal function) | the `__toString` exception |
| instance property | the `__toString` exception |
| static property | the `__toString` exception |
| **return** | `TypeError: r(): Return value must be of type string, C returned`, with the exception as its **previous** |

The return case is worth stating plainly because it looks like a bug and is
not: the method *does* run, it *does* throw, and the TypeError still comes out
in front of it. `getPrevious()` is where the original goes.

`checkType` returns `(value, bool)` with nowhere to put an error, so the throw
is parked on the context -- the mechanism already there for a user error
handler that throws -- and each site that was about to report a type error asks
for it first. A site that forgets still behaves correctly, one opcode late: the
interpreter loop picks up a parked error at the next boundary.

### A shutdown function's exception is an ordinary exception

`register_shutdown_function(function () { throw ...; })` reaches
`set_exception_handler`'s handler. Only one nothing handles is fatal, and that
one **stops** the sequence -- where a handled one lets the remaining shutdown
functions run. Probed both ways. php2go printed the fatal unconditionally and
carried on to the next function, so it got both halves wrong at once.

The shutdown call also needed the `[internal function]` frame that round 277
gave the exception handler and the destructor sweep; the engine calls all three
from C.

## 2026-08-29 -- what the compiler folds is what the evaluator never sees

Interpreter track, round 279.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,258 | **4,261** |
| failed | 297 | 294 |
| unsupported | 156 | 156 |
| errored | 2 | 2 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `bug79947`, `class_constant_inheritance_mutable_data`, `closure_059`.
None newly failing. Differential cases 995 -> 998.

### `1 % 1.5` was the string "11.5"

The constant-expression evaluator ended its operator switch with
`return php.Concat(a, b)`, so every opcode it had no case for -- `ZEND_DIV`,
`ZEND_MOD`, `ZEND_SL`, `ZEND_SR` -- silently concatenated. It survived because
**the compiler folds anything that raises no diagnostic**: `7 % 2` never
reaches the evaluator at all, and only an expression like `1 % 1.5`, which owes
a precision deprecation, is left as an AST. The evaluator's coverage was
therefore never exercised by the ordinary cases.

The runtime compound-assignment path had the full table, including the
`DivisionByZeroError` and `ArithmeticError` cases. Both now go through one
`applyBinary`, and an operator with no entry is an honest `UnsupportedError`
rather than a plausible wrong answer.

Same test, second line: the deprecation was reported **twice**, once per class.
The engine evaluates an unfoldable initializer once and keeps the result on the
declaring class, so reading the constant through a subclass does not evaluate
it again. `Unit.constantValues`, keyed by the declaring class and the name --
an inherited constant is flattened into every subclass's table but evaluated
once.

### A trampoline has no call site

`, called in FILE on line N` is appended to an argument TypeError when the
caller is a script frame. Reaching a closure through `Closure::__invoke` puts an
engine-built trampoline in between, and the clause disappears:

```
$f($b)                             -> ... B given, called in FILE on line 6
$f->__invoke($b)                   -> ... B given
call_user_func([$f,"__invoke"],$b) -> ... B given
call_user_func($f, $b)             -> ... B given, called in FILE on line 9
```

`pendingCall.invokedAs` (round 272) already marked the array form; the direct
`->__invoke()` needed marking too, and both now set
`pendingFrame.viaTrampoline`, which the frame carries as `callerInternal`.

### Also

A compound assignment now checks the offset type before using it, the way a
plain read does: `$a[[1]] += 1` is
`TypeError: Cannot access offset of type array on array`, where php2go had
stringified the array into the key `"Array"` and warned about a missing one.

### Looked at, left alone

`bug76383` wants `array_map` over `$GLOBALS`. Two separate gaps behind it:
php2go's globals table has no `_GET`/`_POST`/`_COOKIE`/`_FILES`, and the
engine's `$GLOBALS` snapshot is not the plain copy php2go makes -- an element
read during the iteration shows the array as it is *then*, not as it was when
the snapshot was taken.

## 2026-08-29 -- a variadic has no name, a key goes first, and null is only for scalars

Interpreter track, round 278.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,254 | **4,258** |
| failed | 300 | 297 |
| unsupported | 156 | 156 |
| errored | 3 | **2** |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed by name: `009`, `ns_077_2`, `variadic/by_ref_error`; one of the three
`errored` cases also cleared. None newly failing. Differential cases
992 -> 995.

### A variadic parameter has no declared name

```c
if (!func || arg_num == 0 || func->common.num_args < arg_num) {
    return NULL;   /* get_function_arg_name */
}
```

`num_args` does **not** count the variadic parameter, so an argument that lands
in a variadic slot has no name to report even though the declaration wrote one
-- and the whole ` ($name)` clause is dropped rather than left empty:

```
function test(&...$args) {}   test(1);   -> test(): Argument #1 could not be passed by reference
function plain(&$x) {}        plain(1);  -> plain(): Argument #1 ($x) could not be passed by reference
```

The same message showed a second difference: `get_function_or_method_name`
always joins with `::`, so an instance call is `K::m()` here where a *trace*
would say `K->m()`. Two different spellings of the same call, and php2go was
using the trace one.

### A constant-expression array evaluates its key first

`[UNKNOWN_KEY => UNKNOWN_VALUE]` reports the **key**, even though the AST holds
the key second and php2go read it in AST order. Only observable when both sides
fail, which is exactly what `ns_077_2` does with
`array(\unknown => unknown)` -- and the two spellings resolve differently
inside a namespace, so the wrong order gave the wrong *name* rather than merely
the wrong one of two identical errors.

### Null for a builtin parameter is a scalar allowance

php2go deprecated null for every non-nullable internal parameter. The engine's
allowance comes from the coercing ZPP macros, so it stops at
`bool|int|float|string`:

```
strlen(null)         Deprecated: ... of type string is deprecated
abs(null)            Deprecated: ... of type int|float is deprecated
count(null)          TypeError: must be of type Countable|array, null given
get_class(null)      TypeError: must be of type object, null given
spl_object_id(null)  TypeError: must be of type object, null given
```

### Noted, not fixed

`temporary_cleaning_017` is now one line from passing and the remaining line is
the destructor-timing family: the engine releases the object at the `return` on
line 10 and attributes the frame there, while php2go still holds it to the
end-of-request sweep, where round 277 correctly gives it an internal frame. The
frame php2go prints is right for the sweep it is doing and wrong for the sweep
the engine did.

## 2026-08-29 -- frames the engine enters on its own, and an ini setting that hides arguments

Interpreter track, round 277.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,249 | **4,254** |
| failed | 305 | 300 |
| unsupported | 156 | 156 |
| errored | 3 | 3 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `exception_handler_002`, `exception_ignore_args`,
`fibers/destructors_008`, `gh10695_4`, `weakrefs/weakmap_dtor_exception`. None
newly failing. Differential cases 990 -> 992.

### Two calls the engine makes that had no frame

`callValueNamed` already pushes an `[internal function]` frame for a callback
invoked from Go -- "the call opcodes push a stack frame; a call made from Go has
to push its own". Two paths went straight to `dispatch` and skipped it:

- the **exception handler**, so an exception thrown *by* the handler reported a
  trace of `#0 {main}` alone where the engine shows
  `#0 [internal function]: {closure:FILE:2}(Object(Exception))`;
- the **end-of-request destructor sweep**. `destructAt` -- the object died at a
  point in the program -- already pushed a frame with that location; `destruct`,
  the shutdown sweep, pushed none. The engine has no script location to
  attribute the sweep to, so the frame is an internal one.

### `zend.exception_ignore_args`

The setting is read where the trace is **captured**, not where it is rendered:
an `ini_set` after the exception was made changes nothing about it. Dropping the
arguments at capture is therefore what makes every rendering agree at once.

It **omits** the `args` key rather than emptying it, which is how a dropped
argument list differs from a call that had none:

```
count($e->getTrace()[0])   ->  4   normally
                           ->  3   under the setting
```

That needed a `StackFrame.ArgsDropped` flag: `Args == nil` cannot say which of
the two it is.

### An oracle limit confirmed

`set_exception_handler` inside the differential harness does not take effect for
an exception escaping the eval -- the engine prints the fatal error instead. The
handler half of a case has to be a `.phpt`; the destructor half is askable.

While writing that case the harness turned up a real divergence that is **not**
fixed here: a local going out of scope at function return is destructed by the
engine *after* the frame is popped, so its trace reads
`#0 FILE(10): ScopedTrace->__destruct()` / `#1 {main}` -- the call site, with
the function already gone. php2go destructs while still inside the function, so
`dropIt()` is still on the stack. Destructor timing, the family already recorded
as out of reach.

### `$v::class` takes an object and nothing else

Not even a class-name string, which every other `$v::` form accepts:

```
$v = "ClassOf";  $v::method();   // fine
$v::class;                       // TypeError: Cannot use "::class" on string
```

php2go shared `classNameOperand` with the static-call opcodes, so a string
answered itself and a scalar earned the generic
`Class name must be a valid object or a string`. The refusal names the value's
type the way `zend_zval_value_name` does -- `true` and `false` rather than
`bool`.

### The other four

- **A class is named as it was declared.** `["stdclass", "b"]()` is
  `Call to undefined method stdClass::b()`; php2go echoed the spelling from the
  callable. Both the error and the `call_user_func` reason go through the class
  entry now.
- **Appending to a string is refused before the operator is.** `$s[] += $s` is
  `[] operator not supported for strings`, not
  `Cannot use assign-op operators with string offsets` -- the second is for a
  *real* offset (`$s[0] += 1`). php2go had one branch for both.
- **`Closure::bindTo` and `Closure::bind` share their parameters** and differ
  only in where they sit, so the argument numbers are an offset rather than two
  copies. `object|string|null` in weak mode takes an int as a class name that
  then does not exist (`Warning: Class "5" not found`); an array has no string
  form and is the TypeError. `Closure::call` grew the `, array given` half of
  its message and the zero-argument `ArgumentCountError`.
- **An exception's message may be an object.** A subclass can redeclare
  `public $message` and put one there; the engine's uncaught report is what
  asks for the string form, so a `__toString` written to compute the message
  lazily runs exactly then. php2go printed `Uncaught MyException` with no
  message at all. The whole `previous` chain is settled, since all of it is
  printed.

## 2026-08-29 -- the loop-carried case: an analysis, an attack suite, and a hole the attacks found

Compiler track. `$s .= $x` in a loop is the half of the builder work where
uniqueness is not in the encoding and has to be proved.

### First, the CFG had to become a graph

Terminators were *strings* -- `br %3, bb1, bb2` -- so no pass could walk the
control-flow graph at all. `Block.Succs` is now populated at the point the
terminator is built, across all 18 terminator sites, and a test parses the block
labels back out of the text and requires them to equal `Succs` in order. Two
encodings of one fact will drift otherwise.

### The measurement, which is what gates the transform

| | CakePHP | `Zend/tests` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| candidate variables (`.=` inside a loop) | 54 | 6 |
| promotable as analysed | 37 (68.5%) | 3 |
| refused by **aliasing** | **0** | 1 |
| refused only by the buffer representation | 17 | 2 |

**Zero aliasing refusals across CakePHP.** Not one string accumulator in the
framework is aliased by `&`, captured by a closure, bound to a global or a
static, passed by reference, or reached by a variable variable. The dangerous
cases the analysis exists to exclude simply do not occur in this code.

### The one refusal that is not about the program

"Read inside the loop" is 17 of 54, and whether it disqualifies depends on the
*target*, not on PHP. It is only fatal if reading the buffer destroys it. Go's
`strings.Builder` snapshots in O(1) and appends only ever write past the length
already handed out, so an earlier `String()` cannot be corrupted -- **checked by
running it**, not by reading the source:

```
snapshot="abc" after further appends, builder="abcXYZ"
snapshot="abc" builder="abcZZZZZZZZZZ"     (after a realloc)
```

So `Reject` carries a `Soft` bit, and for a Go target **100% of CakePHP's
candidates are promotable**. That is the concrete form of the point that
convergence depends on the target's cost model: the same IR analysis gives 68.5%
or 100% depending on what the buffer is.

### The attack suite found a real hole

Eleven functions, one per way of defeating the analysis, each of which must be
refused for the stated reason. One was **promoted**: `$$name`.

The cause was a lowering defect, not an analysis one. `ZEND_FETCH_R`/`_W` on a
local is *always* a variable variable -- verified against the engine, where
`$$name = 1` compiles to `FETCH_W` with the name in op1 while `${"lit"}` is
folded to an ordinary CV and never gets there. The lowering rendered it
`local.get $name`, **indistinguishable from reading a variable actually called
`$name`**, so the frame-opacity check could not see it. It is now `dynvar.get` /
`dynvar.ref`.

Worth stating plainly: the corpus numbers did not move when this was fixed,
because no function in either corpus combines a loop-carried append with a
variable variable. A measurement would never have found it. The attack case did,
which is the whole argument for writing tests designed to break a claim rather
than to confirm it.

### What is not done

The **rewrite**. There is no emitter and `runtime/php` has no buffer type, so a
promotion could not be executed or graded -- it would be an unvalidatable
transform. The plan gates D3 behind exactly this measurement, and the
measurement now exists. The remaining decisions are the ones already recorded as
convergence: where the buffer materialises, and whether a snapshot per read is
cheaper than the O(n²) it removes.

Coverage unchanged at 6,730/6,782 and 10,481/10,780; `go test ./...` green.

## 2026-08-29 -- which class a refusal names, and how often a conversion is reported

Interpreter track, round 275. Five tests, four causes.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,238 | **4,243** |
| failed | 316 | 311 |
| unsupported | 156 | 156 |
| errored | 3 | 3 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `bug44141`, `bug50005`, `bug63173`, `bug64821.3`, `resource_key`. None
newly failing. Differential cases 984 -> 986.

### A constructor refusal names the class that declared it

`new Y` where `Y extends X` and X declares a private `__construct` is
`Call to private X::__construct() from scope Y`. php2go named the class being
instantiated. Two sites: `ZEND_NEW` and the attribute instantiation beside it.

`ReflectionClass::newInstance` is the interesting one, because it produces
*two different* diagnostics and which one depends on a fake scope:

```c
EG(fake_scope) = ce;
constructor = Z_OBJ_HT_P(return_value)->get_constructor(Z_OBJ_P(return_value));
EG(fake_scope) = old_scope;
if (constructor) {
    if (!(constructor->common.fn_flags & ZEND_ACC_PUBLIC)) {
        zend_throw_exception_ex(reflection_exception_ptr, 0,
            "Access to non-public constructor of class %s", ...);
```

The lookup runs with the scope set to the *reflected class*. A private
constructor the class **declares** is visible from there, so `get_constructor`
returns it and the reflector's own refusal fires:
`ReflectionException: Access to non-public constructor of class C`. One the
class **inherited** is not visible even from its own scope, so the lookup itself
fails and the ordinary
`Error: Call to private X::__construct() from scope Heir` comes out -- naming
the reflected class as the scope, which is what makes the two distinguishable.
php2go ran the constructor in both cases.

### The rest

- **A two-element array under the wrong keys.** `[1 => 0, 2 => 0]()` is
  `Array callback has to contain indices 0 and 1`, not the length complaint;
  php2go read index 0 as an absent value and reported `Class "" not found`. The
  `call_user_func` wording is the same sentence lowercased.
- **`thrown in Unknown`.** The trailer of an uncaught fatal is printed by
  `zend_error`, which says `Unknown` for a file it does not have. The
  exception's own `(string)` form leaves the same value empty, so the two lines
  of one report disagree by design.
- **A resource offset is converted once per fetch.** `$a[$r]++` warned twice:
  `elementRef` converts the offset, and then `noteWriteTarget` converted the
  same operand again to record where the slot came from. The second is
  bookkeeping and now passes a nil context.

### Two things left alone

`bug80037` wants `&string(3) "foo"` printed *without* the `&` because the
reference's last other holder is gone -- refcount visibility, already recorded
as out of reach. `gh20177` is the private-property mangling family.

### An oracle limit found

A differential case cannot `fopen(__FILE__)`: the engine side runs with
`__FILE__` set to `php2go-eval`, which is not a path, so the open fails with
`PHP Request Startup: Failed to open stream`. Anything needing a real file
handle has to be a `.phpt`.

## 2026-08-29 -- the structural half of the builder work, and a number I had wrong

Compiler track. Ropes now lower to an explicit string builder rather than a
chain of pure concats.

```
%4:*strbuf = strbuf.new "x"
%5:*strbuf = strbuf.append %4, $a     ; consumes %4 -- same storage
%9:*str    = strbuf.finish %8
```

### The engine's encoding already says it is a builder

I expected to argue that a rope accumulator is structurally unique. The opline
dump settles it without argument:

```
5   ZEND_ROPE_INIT  op2=CONST  result=TMP:8   ext=7
6   ZEND_ROPE_ADD   op1=TMP:8  op2=CV:0  result=TMP:8   ext=1
...
11  ZEND_ROPE_END   op1=TMP:8  op2=CONST result=TMP:7   ext=6
```

**`ROPE_ADD`'s result slot is its own op1** -- the opcode *is* an in-place
append. The slot is a TMP the compiler made for one literal, which no PHP
expression can name, so no `&` can reach it. Nothing is inferred here.

`ZEND_CONCAT` is a different opcode entirely and stays a pure binary op. That
distinction did not exist in the IR before: both lowered to `concat`.

### The claim is measured, not asserted

The whole point of the structural half is that the buffer never escapes, so that
was checked rather than stated: over both corpora, **1,919 buffer definitions,
every one consumed by a builder op, zero escapes**. It is also a test, over three
fixtures, asserting no `*strbuf` value reaches any instruction but
`strbuf.append`/`strbuf.finish` in operand position 0.

(The first version of that scan reported hundreds of escapes. All of them were
`strbuf.finish` lines whose `%n:*str = ` prefix my classifier failed to strip --
the checker was wrong, not the IR. Worth recording because a verification script
that is wrong in the *permissive* direction would have been invisible.)

### A number I gave was wrong

I said the split was "3,240 sites free against 287 needing D3". That counted all
2,273 `concat` sites as free, when most were plain `$a . $b` and not builders at
all, and it left out `array.new` and `array.set`. Correct figures for CakePHP,
now that ropes are separable:

| | sites |
|---|---|
| structurally unique builders (`array.new/set/append`, `strbuf.new/append`) | **5,441** |
| pure binary `concat` -- genuinely two values | 1,716 |
| `assign_op op=concat` -- `$s .= $x`, the D3 case | 287 |

So the free half is larger than I said and the reasoning that produced the old
number was wrong in both directions.

### What this does not decide, which is most of it

Making the builder explicit says it *is* a builder. It does not say what it
should converge to, and that is not a local question:

- **Where `strbuf.finish` belongs.** It sits where `ROPE_END` was -- conservative
  and always correct. Sinking or eliding it needs to know what the consumer does
  with the string: the call graph plus escape analysis.
- **Whether a buffer is worth it at all.** A cost question, and the corpus says
  it is the *common* case rather than a tail: **53% of CakePHP rope chains and
  72% of `Zend/tests` ones are three pieces**, where a builder is four
  instructions and an allocation against two `concat`s. 99% are seven or fewer.
- **Whether the buffer survives a loop iteration**, which is the case that
  actually fixes the O(n²) -- and that belongs to the program-variable half.

Doing the structural half first is what makes the rest a rewrite over named
instructions rather than a rediscovery problem: against pure `concat` chains, D3
would have to first work out that seven concats were one interpolation.

### Gate

Coverage unchanged -- CakePHP 6,730/6,782, `Zend/tests` 10,481/10,780 -- which is
what a pure representation change should do. `go test ./...` fully green,
including `runtime/interp`. Reverting ropes to concat chains fails three tests.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,234 | **4,238** |
| failed | 320 | 316 |
| unsupported | 156 | 156 |
| errored | 3 | 3 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `closure_005`, `closure_038`, `closure_041`, `closure_062`. None newly
failing. Differential cases 982 -> 984.

### A static closure written inside a method has no $this

`static function () {}` declared in an instance method does not capture the
enclosing `$this`: the engine leaves `this_ptr` undef. php2go bound it anyway,
which mattered only where the *absence* is observable -- unbinding.

```c
} else if (!is_fake_closure && !Z_ISUNDEF(closure->this_ptr)
        && (func->common.fn_flags & ZEND_ACC_USES_THIS)) {
    zend_error(E_WARNING, "Cannot unbind $this of closure using $this");
```

Both halves have to hold. A static closure whose body writes `$this` still has
`ZEND_ACC_USES_THIS` set, so the flag alone is not the test -- and php2go,
having bound a `$this` it should not have, warned where the engine is silent.
Three tests turned on this one line.

### A trace names what the closure is bound to

The prefix is the *scope*, not the declaring class, and there is a third case
beyond the two php2go had:

```
$made = (new A)->make();
$made()                              -> A->{closure:A::make():2}()
$made->bindTo(new B, null)           -> Closure->{closure:A::make():2}()
$made->bindTo(new B, "B")            -> B->{closure:A::make():2}()
static function () {}                -> {closure:FILE:8}()
```

`bindTo($obj, null)` keeps the `$this` and drops the scope, so there is no class
to name -- and the trace names the one the value actually is, `Closure`.

## 2026-08-29 -- where a callable is parsed, and what a fetch type decides

Interpreter track, round 273. Six tests, from four unrelated causes.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,228 | **4,234** |
| failed | 326 | 320 |
| unsupported | 156 | 156 |
| errored | 3 | 3 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `property_hooks/gh15644`, `bug41026`, `bug81377`, `bug81684`,
`first_class_callable_signature`, `isset_003`. None newly failing.
Differential cases 978 -> 982.

### A set hook is not a way around private(set)

`public private(set) string $p { set => $value; }` written to from global scope
is `Cannot modify private(set) property C::$p`, and php2go dispatched straight
to the hook. Asymmetric visibility is checked *before* the hooks run -- a set
hook is the implementation of the write, not a replacement for the rule -- and
a hooked property with no set hook is checked the same way. Three write sites
needed it: plain assign, compound assign, and increment.

### `self` in a callable is resolved by the callable parser

Two halves of the same fact, and php2go had both wrong in opposite directions.

```
class T extends P {
  static function main() {
    $a = ["self", "m"];
    $a();                    // Error: Class "self" not found
    call_user_func($a);      // Deprecated: Use of "self" in callables ... then T::m
  }
}
```

The keyword handling lives in the `callable` ZPP, not in the opcode: a bare
`$f(...)` looks the name up as a class and does not find one. php2go resolved
keywords on both paths, so it ran the call the engine refuses.

The other half is *when*: the engine resolves the callable where it validates
the argument, not where it calls it. A shutdown function outlives the scope that
named it, so `register_shutdown_function(["self", "m"])` had to be settled at
registration -- php2go stored the raw array and found nothing at shutdown, so
`bug41026`'s callback never ran and its deprecation never appeared.

The oracle cannot be asked about this one directly:
`register_shutdown_function` with a resolved scope **segfaults the shared
engine** during `php_embed_shutdown`, so the probe has to stop at registration
and the `.phpt` is the check.

### The fetch type decides whether a missing global is reported

`$GLOBALS["x"]` does not compile to an array access; it is a fetch by name
against the global symbol table, and the *type* of that fetch is what says
whether a name that is not there is a diagnostic:

| opcode | written as | missing name |
|---|---|---|
| `ZEND_FETCH_R` | `$GLOBALS["x"]` | `Warning: Undefined global variable $x` |
| `ZEND_FETCH_IS` | `??`, `isset()` | silent -- the absence *is* the answer |
| `ZEND_FETCH_RW` | `$GLOBALS["x"] .= ...` | reported, in the global wording |
| `ZEND_FETCH_W` | `$GLOBALS["x"] = ...` | created in silence |
| `ZEND_FETCH_UNSET` | `unset($GLOBALS["x"]["k"])` | silent, **and not created** |

php2go reported for everything that was not a W or RW fetch, which is where
`bug81684` (`??=`) and `bug81377` (`unset` of a sub-key) came from. The UNSET
form needed its own branch rather than joining the by-reference ones: taking a
reference to the slot would grow the table, and the engine leaves it alone.

### A Closure dumps as `Closure [`

`(string) new ReflectionFunction(test(...))` is `Closure [ <user> function test
]`, not `Function [`. The subject being a `Closure` changes only the leading
word -- the rest still says `function` or `public method` as the declaration
does -- and it holds however the closure was made, including a first-class
callable that reflection answers for by the name it wraps.

## 2026-08-29 -- append is not one operation, and the naming question was the wrong question

Compiler track, design. I had filed a tidy-up: `IR-ASSEMBLY.md` lists the place
families as `dim`, `prop`, `sprop`, `local`, `append`, while `internal/lower`
emits `dim.append` — spelled two ways, pick one. That framing was wrong, and the
correction is worth more than the rename would have been.

**Append is already four instructions, and they do not share a shape.** Counted
over CakePHP:

| form | sites | shape |
|---|---|---|
| `%n = concat %a, %b` | 2,273 | defines a value — a rope |
| `%n = array.append %acc, %v` | 967 | defines a value — an array literal |
| `%n:place = dim.append %c` + `store` | 563 | writes a place — `$a[] = v` |
| `assign_op $s, %v, op=concat` | 287 | writes a place — `$s .= $x` |

Two define values, two write places. So `append` was never a place family, and
the spec is what was wrong, not the code. Corrected there.

### The pure/mutating choice is a property of the operands, not the syntax

```
strbuf ← (str | strbuf)     mutating; the destination is uniquely owned
str    + (str | strbuf)     pure; produces a new string
```

Four operand combinations, two result shapes, and the same duality for arrays —
`array.append` on `*Array!` mutates, on `*Array&` it clones first.

### Which rules out doing it as a specialization

`.<spec>` was reserved for D4 to pick a cheaper implementation of the *same*
instruction: `add.i64` still defines a value. **The builder transform does not
preserve shape.** Rewriting `%n = concat %a, %b` into an in-place append to `%a`
deletes `%n`'s definition, promotes `%a` from operand to destination, and forces
every consumer of `%n` to read `%a` instead — with `%a` dead afterwards. That is
a graph rewrite belonging to D3, and the D4 specialization table cannot express
it. Recorded in `IR-DESIGN.md`; the plan had this filed under D3.2 as if it were
a table entry.

### And it splits the O(n²) string problem in two

The two sources of builders carry different proof obligations:

- **Compiler-invented accumulators** — rope chains and array literals. The
  accumulator is a TMP the compiler made for one literal and consumed in the next
  opline of the group, and **no PHP expression can name it**, so no `&` can reach
  it. Uniqueness is structural. These can be built in place with no escape
  analysis at all.
- **Program variables** — `$s .= $x` in a loop, the case that is asymptotically
  wrong today. Aliasing, closure capture and references to typed properties are
  all live questions here, and every uniqueness claim owes a differential case
  built to break it.

So the free half is 3,240 sites (`concat` + `array.append`) and the half needing
D3 is 287. That ratio is the argument for doing the structural half first and
independently.

### No code changed

The lowering emits the right things already; only the specification and the plan
were describing them wrongly.

## 2026-08-29 -- four small diagnostics, one of them ordered wrongly

Interpreter track, round 272. Four unrelated one- and two-line diffs, picked off
an EXPECTF-aware clustering of the whole corpus rather than a single family.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,224 | **4,228** |
| failed | 330 | 326 |
| unsupported | 156 | 156 |
| errored | 3 | 3 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

Fixed: `class_alias_014`, `gh15976/alias-names`, `named_params/
internal_variadics`, `closure_invoke_ref_warning`. None newly failing.
Differential cases 975 -> 978.

### An engine variadic does not collect names

`array_merge([1, 2], a: [3, 4])` is
`ArgumentCountError: array_merge() does not accept unknown named parameters`,
and php2go accepted it silently. The rule is not about the function: it is
about which ZPP macro the declaration used.

```c
#define Z_PARAM_VARIADIC_EX(...)  /* ... */     if (UNEXPECTED(ZEND_CALL_INFO(execute_data) & ZEND_CALL_HAS_EXTRA_NAMED_PARAMS)) {         _error_code = ZPP_ERROR_UNEXPECTED_EXTRA_NAMED; ```

`Z_PARAM_VARIADIC_WITH_NAMED` keeps them instead, and only nine declarations in
the whole tree use it -- `call_user_func`, `Closure::__invoke`,
`Closure::call`, `Fiber::start`, and the four Reflection invokers. Every one is
a forwarder, which is the same list `named-arguments.md` already had for
"which builtins forward names"; it is now a map in `call.go` rather than
scattered knowledge.

**The count is checked first.** A first version of this refused before the
arity check and broke `named_params/call_user_func_array_variadic`, where
`call_user_func_array("array_multisort", ["" => 1])` must answer
`array_multisort() expects at least 1 argument, 0 given` -- the engine's
`ZEND_PARSE_PARAMETERS_START` compares `_num_args` against the minimum before
it ever reaches the variadic macro, and `_num_args` counts only the arguments
that landed in a slot. Guarding the refusal on `given >= required` restores the
order.

### The rest

- **`class_alias` has no `class_alias():` prefix.** Both of its diagnostics go
  through `zend_error`, not `zend_argument_error`, so the message is plain
  `Warning: Class "bar" not found`. php2go had added the prefix most builtins
  do carry.
- **`class_alias($x, "_")` is deprecated since 8.4.** Exactly one underscore;
  `"__"` is fine.
- **`[$closure, "__invoke"]` names the trampoline.** Probed:

  ```
  call_user_func([$c, "__invoke"], null)  -> Closure::__invoke(): Argument #1 ($arg) ...
  call_user_func($c, null)                -> {closure:FILE:2}(): Argument #1 ($arg) ...
  ```

  The array form reaches the closure through `Closure::__invoke`, so a
  diagnostic raised against the call names that -- while a *backtrace* still
  shows the closure's own compiled name (the engine shows both frames:
  `{closure:...}()` called from `Closure->__invoke()`). `pendingCall.invokedAs`
  carries the difference, with `diagnosticName` / `diagnosticTraceName` beside
  `traceName` so the trace is left alone.

### Tooling

The triage lens this round was a clustering script that expands EXPECTF into a
regex before diffing, so `object(C)#3` no longer reads as a difference from
`object(C)#%d`. A plain text diff of the same dump ranked twenty tests as
"large" that were in fact one line apart. It lives in the job workspace, not in
the tree.

## 2026-08-29 -- a namespaced call names two functions, and the IR was keeping one

Compiler track. Closing the second item filed with the six opcodes.

`implode()` written inside `namespace App\Support` does not mean one function.
PHP resolves `App\Support\implode` if it exists and the global `implode`
otherwise, and the compiler stores **three consecutive literals** for it:

```
0  string "App\Support\implode"     <- as written; op2 names this one
1  string "app\support\implode"     <- lowercased, namespaced
2  string "implode"                   <- the unqualified fallback
```

`ZEND_INIT_NS_FCALL_BY_NAME`'s op2 names only the first, and the lowering kept
only that -- so the IR asserted a call to `App\Support\implode`, a function
that in CakePHP's case never exists. **6,440 call sites in CakePHP alone**, all
of them claiming a resolution PHP does not perform.

They now carry both: `call.fn "App\Support\implode"(...), fallback="implode"`.
The attribute form is what the assembly grammar already allows; `.<spec>` is
reserved for Phase D4's specialization suffixes and could not be used.

### The offset was checked at scale, not assumed

The `+2` was read off one probe, so it was verified rather than trusted. Across
both corpora, **6,842 fallbacks, of which zero are qualified and zero contain an
uppercase letter** -- which is what the third literal is defined to be, and what
a wrong offset could not have produced. No body bails on a missing fallback
literal either, so the run is always three.

Two boundary cases confirmed against the engine while probing: a **fully
qualified** call (`\str_repeat()`) compiles to `INIT_FCALL_BY_NAME` and never
reaches this opcode, so it correctly gets no fallback; and a **first-class
callable** (`strtoupper(...)`) resolves the same pair, so `closure.from_call`
carries it too.

### Also

`php2harvest` now dumps the literal table. The runs above are invisible without
it -- the opline shows `CONST:0` and nothing more -- and this is the second time
in two days that reading an encoding needed a dump the tool did not produce.

### Gate

`gofmt`, build, vet and tests clean for `internal/...` and my commands. **`go
build ./...` currently fails in `runtime/interp`** -- `closure.go:600: unknown
field invokedAs in struct literal of type pendingCall` -- which is the other
session mid-edit: that file was written seconds before the check, the field is
theirs to add, and `runtime/interp` imports nothing of mine. The two
`pendingCall` types are unrelated (`runtime/interp/call.go:26` is theirs,
`internal/lower/lower.go:87` is mine). `cmd/php2eval` and `cmd/php2phpt` fail
only because they import that package.

## 2026-08-29 -- lazy objects: dynamic properties, and the readonly a reset keeps

Interpreter track, round 271. Four `lazy_objects` tests, all reached through
`ReflectionProperty`.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,220 | **4,224** |
| failed | 334 | 330 |
| unsupported | 156 | 156 |
| errored | 3 | 3 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

`lazy_objects/` went 186 -> **190** of 220 attempted. Diff-set against round
270: four fixed (`reset_as_lazy_readonly`,
`setRawValueWithoutLazyInitialization_readonly`, and the two
`*_no_dynamic_prop`), none newly failing. Differential cases 970 -> 975.

### A dynamic property is reflectable through its object

`new ReflectionProperty($obj, "dyn")` succeeds when the *object* grew the
property, and fails through the class name. Probed:

```
$dyn->getName()   -> "dyn"       $dyn->isDynamic()  -> true
$dyn->class       -> "C"         $dyn->isDefault()  -> false
(string) $dyn     -> Property [ <dynamic> public $dyn ]
new ReflectionProperty("C", "dyn") -> ReflectionException: Property C::$dyn does not exist
```

php2go refused the constructor outright, which is what made both
`*_no_dynamic_prop` tests fail: they never reached the call they were testing.
`reflector.dynamic` now carries the distinction and the reflector holds a
synthesized `pb.Property`.

Two things fell out on the way. `declaredProperty` deliberately skips statics,
so `new ReflectionProperty("C", "s")` could not find one either -- reflection
now goes through `reflectableProperty`, which sees them. And
`ReflectionProperty::isInitialized` was simply missing; the engine wants an
argument even when the reflector was built from an object
(`Argument #1 ($object) must be provided for instance properties`), because it
keeps no reference to it.

### A reset keeps a final class's readonly value

`resetAsLazyGhost` unsets the declared properties so the initializer can write
them again. `zend_lazy_objects.c` makes one exception:

```c
if ((prop_info->flags & ZEND_ACC_READONLY) && !(Z_PROP_FLAG_P(p) & IS_PROP_REINITABLE)
        && ((obj->ce->ce_flags & ZEND_ACC_FINAL) || (prop_info->flags & ZEND_ACC_FINAL))) {
    continue;
}
```

A readonly property that already holds a value survives the reset when the
object's class is final -- no subclass can reach it, so nothing could
legitimately write it again -- and the reconstructing `__construct` is then
refused with `Cannot modify readonly property B::$a`. That is the whole
difference between the `B` and `final class C extends B` halves of
`reset_as_lazy_readonly`.

Keeping the value is not enough on its own. The kept property must also be
marked **not deferred**, or the ghost's `restoreDefaults` pass wipes it on the
way into the initializer; that mark is the same `Lazy.Skipped` that
`skipLazyInitialization` sets. Once it is set, `allSkipped` handles the tail
case for free: reset a final class whose *only* property is a kept readonly one
and there is nothing left to defer, so the object is not lazy and the
initializer never runs. The engine does the same thing through
`lazy_properties_count`, and a first attempt here that special-cased "cleared
nothing" was the wrong shape for the same effect.

`setRawValueWithoutLazyInitialization` also had to grow the plain readonly
refusal: writing the raw value is still a write. `skipLazyInitialization`
writes nothing and is never refused -- calling it twice on a readonly property
is fine.

### Found but not fixed

The differential caught an arity gap while checking the dynamic-property
refusals: `ReflectionProperty::skipLazyInitialization()` takes exactly one
argument and the engine says
`ArgumentCountError: ... expects exactly 1 argument, 2 given`, where php2go
accepts the extra one. Engine-method arity is unchecked across the board, so it
is recorded in TODO rather than patched here.

## 2026-08-29 -- the five impossible bails: inlining splices oplines out of their block

Compiler track. Follow-up to the six opcodes, closing the item filed there as
"suspicious rather than missing".

`ZEND_ASSIGN_OBJ (no OP_DATA follows)` stopped five CakePHP bodies, and an
OP_DATA always follows that opcode -- so the pass was losing track rather than
meeting an unmodelled construct. The trace named it in one read:

```
28  ZEND_FAST_CALL   op1=0:32          # splices the finally body, oplines 32..34
...
32  ZEND_ASSIGN_OBJ  op1=0:...  op2=1:15
33  ZEND_OP_DATA     op1=8:2
34  ZEND_FAST_RET
  leaders=[0 9 18 29 30 31 32 35]  block=18..28
```

The `FAST_CALL` at 28 belongs to the block `18..28`, and inlining prepends
oplines 32 and 33 to that block's work queue. `opData()` then asked whether the
OP_DATA was within `[start, end]` -- `33 > 28` -- and concluded it was missing,
while it sat immediately after its own opline in the op_array.

**Inlining splices oplines from outside the current block into it, so anything
bounded by the block rather than by the opline stream is wrong.** An OP_DATA is
glued to the opline before it and is never a jump target, so the block it lands
in is irrelevant; the bound is `len(oplines)`.

The risk in loosening it was the opposite failure -- an OP_DATA becoming a block
leader and being lowered on its own -- so that was checked rather than argued:
**neither corpus produces a single `OP_DATA reached on its own` bail**, before or
after.

In source terms this was `$this->last = 'done'` inside a `finally`, which is now
a fixture. Reverting the bound makes both the targeted test and the golden fail
with the original message.

### Result

| corpus | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CakePHP `src/` | 6,725 / 6,782 = 99.2% | **6,730 / 6,782 = 99.2%** |
| `Zend/tests` | 10,480 / 10,780 = 97.2% | **10,481 / 10,780 = 97.2%** |

Five bodies and one, so the rates do not move. What moves is the shape of what
is left: **CakePHP's remaining 52 bails are now every one of them an unmodelled
opcode**, with no "the pass lost track" entries at all --

```
MATCH 19   SWITCH_STRING 11   MATCH_ERROR 8   DEFINED 5
COPY_TMP 3   VERIFY_NEVER_TYPE 3   ADD_ARRAY_UNPACK 1   BW_NOT 1   DISCARD_EXCEPTION 1
```

-- which is the honest tail the `unsupported` bucket is supposed to be.

### Not addressed

`INIT_NS_FCALL_BY_NAME` still renders only its namespaced literal, dropping the
global fallback the encoding carries. It blocks no body and is a fidelity gap
rather than a lost-track bug, so it stays filed.

## 2026-08-29 -- closures under reflection: scope, trampoline, and target

Interpreter track, round 270. Four related gaps, all around what a `Closure`
looks like from the reflection API.

### Result

Corpus `Zend/tests`, same binary and command before and after
(`php2phpt -diff 1300 third_party/php-src/Zend/tests`, retried until
`0 compile-error`):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passed | 4,216 | **4,220** |
| failed | 338 | 334 |
| unsupported | 154 | 156 |
| errored | 3 | 3 |
| attempted | 4,713 | 4,713 |

`attributes/` went 86 -> **90** of 94 attempted. Diff-set comparison against
round 269: four tests fixed (`attributes/013_class_scope`,
`attributes/017_closure_scope`, `attributes/031_backtrace`,
`attributes/deprecated/functions/gh17866`), none newly failing.
Differential cases 965 -> 970.

### What was wrong

**1. A closure's attributes were evaluated with no scope.** `#[A(self::FOO)]`
written on a closure declared inside a class has to resolve `self` against that
class -- and against the *rebound* class after `bindTo`. The
`ReflectionFunction` constructor now records `fn.class` on the reflector.

**2. A deprecated closure was named twice.** `noteDeprecatedCallAs` formats
`"Method %s::%s()"` from the scope and an `as` name, and the closure call sites
passed `closureTraceName(...)`, which already carries `Foo->`. The message came
out `Method Foo::Foo->__invoke()`. A closure that wraps a method is reported as
that method, so the `as` is now the plain function name whenever the closure
has a scope; a scopeless closure keeps the trace name, which is what the engine
prints for it (`Function {closure:FILE:LINE}()`).

Two call sites, and only one of them was live: `runtime/interp/call.go` (the
callback/handler path) and `runtime/interp/interp.go` (`DO_FCALL`). Fixing the
first alone changed nothing, which is worth remembering -- the deprecation for
a directly-invoked closure comes out of `DO_FCALL`.

**3. `ReflectionMethod($closure, "__invoke")` reflected the wrong thing.**
`Closure` declares no `__invoke`; `zend_get_closure_invoke_method` hands back a
**trampoline** that carries the wrapped function's parameters, attributes and
deprecation under the name and scope of `Closure`, as an *internal*
declaration. Probed:

```
$c = (new Foo)->bar(...);          // Foo::bar has #[\Deprecated] and int $z = 3
$rc = new ReflectionMethod($c, "__invoke");
getName()                -> "__invoke"      (not "bar")
class / getDeclaringClass -> "Closure"      (not "Foo")
isDeprecated()           -> true            (from the wrapped function)
getParameters()[0]       -> $z              (from the wrapped function)
(string) $rc             -> Method [ <internal, deprecated> public method __invoke ] {
                              - Parameters [1] { Parameter #0 [ <optional> int $z = <default> ] }
                            }
```

An earlier attempt in this round reflected the *wrapped* method instead
(`getName()` -> `"bar"`, class -> `"Foo"`); that made `gh17866` pass and was
still wrong, and the differential caught it. `reflector.trampoline` now carries
the distinction, and `functionString`/`parameterString` grew an `internal`
flag: no `@@` line, `<internal>` rather than `<user>`, and `= <default>`
instead of the value, since an internal declaration keeps no `RECV_INIT` to
read the default back from.

**4. An attribute on a closure targets a function, not a method.** Fix 1
regressed `attributes/gh8421`: giving the reflector a scope made
`functionTarget` call it a method, so `#[Attribute(Attribute::TARGET_FUNCTION)]`
on a closure declared in a class was refused. The engine's test is not "has a
scope":

```c
if (fptr->common.scope && (fptr->common.fn_flags & (ZEND_ACC_CLOSURE|ZEND_ACC_FAKE_CLOSURE)) != ZEND_ACC_CLOSURE) {
    target = ZEND_ATTRIBUTE_TARGET_METHOD;
```

A closure *written as one* has `ZEND_ACC_CLOSURE` alone and targets a function
even with a scope; a first-class callable of a method is a **fake** closure --
both bits -- and targets a method. php2go already tracked that as
`closure.fake`, so `reflector.realClosure` is `!fn.fake`.

### Also fixed on the way

- `ReflectionAttribute` now sets its declared `public readonly string $name`,
  so `var_dump` of one shows `["name"]=> string(10) "Deprecated"` rather than
  `uninitialized(string)`. This was the rest of `gh17866`'s diff.
- Every reflector refuses a write to `$name` or `$class` with
  `ReflectionException: Cannot set read-only property C::$p`. That is
  `_reflection_write_property`, a two-name check on any class that declares the
  property -- not a `readonly` flag, so it applies from every scope. php2go was
  silently accepting the write.

**5. A reflector cut the anonymous-class name at its NUL.** `getName()`,
`getShortName()` and the declared `$name` all went through `php.DisplayName`,
so `(new ReflectionObject($anon))->getName() === get_class($anon)` was false.
Cutting at the NUL is what a *diagnostic* does -- the engine's messages are
printf and each interpolated C string ends there -- and reflection is not a
diagnostic. It answers with the real name, `class@anonymous\0file:line$hash`
and all, which is why the comparison holds. `getShortName()` needs no special
case: the mangled name has no backslash to split on.

### Trap worth recording

`Raise("ReflectionException", ...)` from inside `checkPropertyWrite` produced an
**uncatchable** failure: `Raise` builds a `*phpError`, which only becomes a
throwable once something calls `materialize`, and the property-write call sites
hand the error straight to `f.raise`. Sibling code in `reflection.go` gets away
with `Raise` because a builtin *method* return goes through `materialize`. From
a property-write path the call has to be `in.throwError(ctx, unit, ...)`, which
builds the object there and then. The symptom is distinctive: php2eval reports
`--- INTERPRETER (error) ---` with the right message and no PHP-level
`Fatal error:` banner at all.

## 2026-08-29 -- the six short-circuit opcodes, and an analysis that did not know what it was analysing

Compiler track, continuing straight on from the Phase C landing.

### Result

| corpus | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CakePHP `src/` | 5,030 / 6,782 = **74.2%** | 6,725 / 6,782 = **99.2%** |
| `Zend/tests` | 10,331 / 10,780 = **95.8%** | 10,480 / 10,780 = **97.2%** |

The six were `JMP_FRAMELESS`, `JMPZ_EX`, `JMPNZ_EX`, `COALESCE`, `JMP_SET` and
`ASSERT_CHECK`, plus `FRAMELESS_ICALL_0..3`, which `JMP_FRAMELESS` is useless
without. They were worth 74.2% -> 98.3% on CakePHP; the last 0.9% came from a
bug they exposed, below.

### All four short-circuit forms have one shape and two meanings

`&&`, `||`, `??` and `?:` compile identically: evaluate op1, and on the
short-circuit path leave a value in the result slot and jump past a fallback
opline that writes *the same slot*. So the slot is defined in two blocks and
read in a third -- which is already a place under the rule that covers any
cross-block temporary. **No block arguments were needed**, contrary to what I
said when scoping this.

What differs is what lands in the slot, and the opcode names do not say. Settled
with `php2eval` against the engine rather than by reading the VM:

```
0 && $b   -> bool(false)      JMPZ_EX  boolifies
1 || $b   -> bool(true)       JMPNZ_EX boolifies
0 ?? $b   -> int(0)           COALESCE copies the value through
"a" ?: $b -> string(1) "a"    JMP_SET  copies the value through
```

Getting that backwards turns every `?:` into a boolean, and nothing about the
opline encoding would have caught it. The mutation was tried: flipping `JMP_SET`
to boolify fails both the targeted test and the golden.

### The frameless call, which names no function

PHP 8.4 compiles some internal calls without a frame. `JMP_FRAMELESS` guards the
fast path -- if the name still resolves to the internal function the compiler had
in mind, jump to it, otherwise fall through to the ordinary three-phase call --
and both arms write the same result slot, so the merge is the same place again.

Two things had to be harvested rather than guessed:

- **`extended_value` is an index into the manifest's `frameless_functions`**, and
  it is keyed per *arity*: `in_array` with two arguments is index 7 and with
  three is index 8. The opcode carries no name at all.
- **`FRAMELESS_ICALL_3` spills its third argument into an `OP_DATA`**, exactly
  like the assignment opcodes, so the un-flattening the pass already does covers
  it.

`ASSERT_CHECK` turned out to be a *run-time* check of the assertions setting, not
a compile-time one, so it lowers to an `assertions_enabled` intrinsic. Folding it
at lowering time would bake the harvesting build's `zend.assertions` into a
standalone artifact.

### The bug the six exposed: an analysis that did not know what it was analysing

With the short-circuit opcodes lowering, the top CakePHP blocker became
`ADD_ARRAY_ELEMENT (array accumulator not live in this block)` at 56 bodies --
a blocker created by fixing another, which is the normal shape of this work.

The cause is worth recording because the fact was already written down twice.
`ZEND_ADD_ARRAY_ELEMENT`'s **result slot is also an input**: the engine reuses it
across a whole array literal. The lowering case says so in a comment and handles
it. But `findCrossBlock` -- the analysis that decides which slots become places
-- counted operands as reads and the result purely as a definition. So an array
literal spanning a block boundary, which is any literal containing a
short-circuit (`[$a ?? $b, $c]`), had an accumulator the analysis believed was
never read.

Teaching it the two opcodes that read what they write took CakePHP from 98.3% to
**99.2%**. The lesson generalises: knowing a fact in the transformation is not the
same as knowing it in the analysis that feeds the transformation, and the second
is where it was missing.

### What is left, and it is a different shape now

CakePHP's remaining 57 bodies: `MATCH` (19), `SWITCH_STRING` (11), `MATCH_ERROR`
(8), `ASSIGN_OBJ (no OP_DATA follows)` (5), `DEFINED` (5), then singletons.
`Zend/tests`'s remaining 300 lead with `INIT_PARENT_PROPERTY_HOOK_CALL` (38),
`DISCARD_EXCEPTION` (28), `BIND_INIT_STATIC_OR_JMP` (27), `SEND_USER` (22).

The jump tables (`MATCH`, `SWITCH_STRING`) are the only coherent group left; the
rest is genuinely a tail. `ASSIGN_OBJ (no OP_DATA follows)` is suspicious rather
than missing -- OP_DATA should always follow -- and is filed as such.

### Also done

`php2harvest` now prints `extended_value` and the smart-branch flag (TODO item,
open since 2026-08-23). It was needed to read these opcodes at all: without it
the dump cannot tell `FRAMELESS_ICALL_2` on `in_array` from the same opcode on
any other function, because the name lives only in that operand.
